picks.title: Retatrutide Once Weekly for Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea.

sections.objective: Retatrutide, an investigational triple agonist of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon-like peptide 1, and glucagon receptors, may be useful for treating obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).
sections.methods: In two phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trials nested within larger basket trials of once-weekly subcutaneous retatrutide, we assigned adults with moderate-to-severe OSA and a body-mass index (the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) of at least 27, without (TRIUMPH-1-OSA) or with (TRIUMPH-2-OSA) type 2 diabetes, to receive retatrutide (4, 9, or 12 mg) or placebo. The primary end point was the change in the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI, the average number of apneas and hypopneas per hour of sleep) at 80 weeks with 9 mg and 12 mg of retatrutide. For OSA-related end points, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy used for participants who had intercurrent events suggesting treatment failure and a treatment-policy strategy used elsewhere. We also report intention-to-treat (ITT) results.
sections.results: A total of 243 participants underwent randomization in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and 448 in TRIUMPH-2-OSA. The baseline mean AHI was 58.6 and 55.9 events per hour, respectively, and the mean body weight was 119.6 and 115.9 kg. At 80 weeks, the mean changes in the AHI (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-1-OSA were -22.9 (4 mg), -34.3 (9 mg), and -31.7 (12 mg) events per hour, versus -9.9 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -13.0 [95% confidence interval {CI}, -23.0 to -3.0], -24.4 [95% CI, -34.1 to -14.7], and -21.9 [95% CI, -32.2 to -11.5], respectively). The changes with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-2-OSA were -19.2 (4 mg), -24.7 (9 mg), and -25.4 (12 mg) events per hour, versus -10.3 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -8.9 [95% CI, -15.9 to -2.0], -14.4 [95% CI, -21.6 to -7.2], and -15.1 [95% CI, -22.5 to -7.7]). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -13.2 (95% CI, -22.6 to -3.9), -24.7 (95% CI, -34.1 to -15.3), and -22.5 (95% CI, -31.9 to -13.1) in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and -8.8 (95% CI, -15.8 to -1.7), -13.9 (95% CI, -21.3 to -6.6), and -15.0 (95% CI, -22.5 to -7.4) in TRIUMPH-2-OSA. The mean percent change in body weight with retatrutide (key secondary end point) was -12.5 to -22.2% in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and -12.1 to -18.5% in TRIUMPH-2-OSA, versus -4.8% and -5.6% with placebo (treatment-regimen estimand). The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal.
sections.conclusion: In adults with OSA and obesity or overweight with or without type 2 diabetes, retatrutide resulted in significantly greater decreases in the AHI than placebo. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-1 and -2 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05929066 and NCT05929079.).

picks.title: Effectiveness of a structured template to improve completeness of reporting randomised trial protocols: randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To evaluate whether providing authors with a manuscript template structured according to the Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials (SPIRIT) 2025 reporting guideline for use during revision improves the completeness of reporting in randomised trial protocols.
sections.methods: Randomised controlled trial. Handling editors asked the intervention group authors to use a SPIRIT based manuscript template when preparing their first revision. The template included structured subheadings corresponding to SPIRIT 2025 items, along with guidance on reporting. Editorial decisions were not conditional on use of the template. Control group manuscripts underwent standard peer review.
sections.results: Of the 70 manuscripts randomised (35 in each group), all were analysed, with no loss to follow-up. In the intervention group, completeness of reporting in randomised trial protocols improved by 0.61 points (95% confidence interval 0.20 to 1.01) compared with the control group, with mean (standard deviation) scores increasing from 5.42 (1.07) to 6.70 (1.23) and 5.77 (1.19) to 6.32 (0.94), respectively. The largest improvements were observed for recruitment, data collection methods, and access to data. Median time to submission of the first revision was similar between the intervention and control groups (27.10 v 29.86 days, respectively). Data on harms were not systematically collected. Among 14 of 35 survey respondents (40%), many (8/13, 62%) reported the template as time consuming and some (5/13, 39%) as burdensome. Most respondents, however, found it easy to use (10/13, 77%), helpful for improving the manuscript (9/13, 69%), and reassuring for adherence to SPIRIT (13/13, 100%).
sections.conclusion: Providing authors of randomised controlled trials with a SPIRIT based template during manuscript revision modestly improved the completeness of reporting in the trial protocols without extending revision times.
sections.other: BMJ Open. 70 of 74 manuscripts screened between 29 April and 27 May 2025 that reported randomised controlled trial protocols with a decision of minor or major revision after the first round of peer review were randomly allocated (1:1) using an R generated sequence. Authors were not informed of the study. The primary outcome was completeness of reporting score in the revised manuscript (adjusted for baseline), calculated as the mean of 11 SPIRIT items that are frequently inadequately reported (each scored 0, 0.5, or 1) and linearly rescaled to a 0-10 score. After submission of their first revision, authors in the intervention group completed an online survey. The survey included both fixed response and open ended questions designed to capture the authors' perceptions of ease of use, helpfulness, and any challenges encountered when using the template. Secondary outcomes included mean completeness of reporting scores for each item, median time to submission of the revised manuscript, and authors' experiences of using the template. Outcome assessors, but not editors or investigators, were masked.

picks.title: Cold activates a BH2 metabolic network promoting longevity and proteostasis
picks.abstract: Abstract Moderately cold temperatures extend lifespan and promote health across species 1–3 , yet the molecular mechanisms underlying these benefits remain unclear. Here we define a metabolite-driven, multi-tissue signalling system that links cold temperature to enhanced longevity and proteostasis in Caenorhabditis elegans . Cold temperature upregulates the biopterin-synthesis enzyme CAT-4 (GCH1 in humans), increasing production of dihydrobiopterin (BH2), a transportable reservoir for the bioactive cofactor tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). BH2 is produced in muscle and transported to distal tissues, including the intestine and neurons, where it is converted into BH4 by the salvage enzyme DHFR-1. BH4 functions as an essential cofactor for phenylalanine hydroxylase PAH-1, promoting tyrosine synthesis and extending lifespan. This BH2–BH4 axis also prevents disease-related protein aggregation and subsequent neuronal dysfunction during ageing. Importantly, increasing BH2 synthesis specifically in muscle is sufficient to promote longevity and suppress pathological protein aggregation in distal tissues, even at normal or elevated temperatures. In human cells, BH2 or tyrosine supplementation reduces aggregation of polyQ-expanded proteins associated with Huntington’s disease, as well as mutant variants of TDP-43 and FUS that cause amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Together, these findings identify BH2 as a cold-induced metabolite of which the synthesis, intertissue transport and conversion into bioactive BH4 preserve organism-wide proteostasis and extend lifespan.

picks.title: Recordanelles for transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording in human cells
picks.abstract: Abstract Transcriptomic measurement technologies provide powerful approaches to understand biology but are limited to providing either a high-resolution snapshot at a moment in time or a low-resolution history of transcription constrained to a few genes over a narrow time range. Here, we introduce the ‘recordanelle’, a single-component synthetic organelle capable of recording the transcriptome in human cells. Recordanelles are composed of a mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein. We demonstrate that the recordanelle can be engineered to recruit engineered RNAs or a sampling of up to 90% of all endogenous mRNAs and protect them over several days. We further show that transient and dynamic transcriptional responses resulting from inducible promoters or interferon signaling are preserved throughout time within the recordanelle at the single-cell level. This work provides a nondisruptive and unbiased transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording technology to enable a deeper understanding of biology.

picks.title: Cardiovascular safety of orforglipron versus insulin glargine in adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk (ACHIEVE-4): a phase 3, event-driven, randomised, open-label, non-inferiority, active comparator trial.

sections.objective: Orforglipron is an oral, non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist. While some peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists have established cardiovascular benefit, the cardiovascular safety of non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists has not been studied. This study aimed to compare the effect of orforglipron with insulin glargine on the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events in individuals with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight who are at increased risk for cardiovascular events.
sections.methods: This event-driven, phase 3, multicentre, randomised, open-label, active comparator, parallel-group study was conducted in 317 sites across 16 countries and territories. Adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk with glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) concentrations between 7·0% and 10·5% (53-91 mmol/mol) and a BMI of 25 kg/m2 or more, treated with up to three glucose-lowering medications (metformin, a sulfonylurea, and/or an SGLT2 inhibitor), were randomly assigned (1:1) to oral orforglipron maximum tolerated dose (up to 36 mg capsule [equivalent to 17·2 mg tablet]) or injectable titrated insulin glargine, each administered once daily. All participants had established cardiovascular or chronic kidney disease. The primary outcome was time to occurrence of four-component major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE-4), including cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for unstable angina. Non-inferiority of orforglipron to insulin glargine was declared if the upper limit of the two-sided 95% CI for the hazard ratio (HR; orforglipron vs insulin glargine) was less than 1·8. The primary endpoint and other safety endpoints were assessed in all participants who took at least one dose of assigned treatment using all datapoints from baseline until withdrawal or study completion, regardless of treatment adherence. This trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05803421) and is completed.
sections.results: Between May 1, 2023, and Sept 5, 2024, 2749 participants were randomly assigned (1371 to orforglipron and 1378 to insulin glargine). 1032 (38%) participants were female and 1717 (62·5%) male. 2362 (85·9%) participants had established cardiovascular disease and 1033 (37·6%) had chronic kidney disease. Mean baseline age, HbA1c, and BMI were 63·1 years (SD 9·9), 8·2% (1·0), and 33 kg/m2 (6·2), respectively. Over a median follow-up of 2 years, the primary outcome occurred in 57 (4·2%) of 1358 orforglipron participants and 67 (5·0%) of 1343 insulin glargine participants, showing non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4 (HR 0·84; 95% CI 0·59-1·20; p<0·0001 for non-inferiority). Gastrointestinal adverse events were reported in 851 (62·1%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 193 (14·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants; clinically significant or severe hypoglycaemia (glucose <3 mmol/L [54 mg/dL]) occurred in 93 (6·8%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 260 (19·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants. 62 deaths were reported during the study: 19 (1·4%) of 1371 participants receiving orforglipron and 43 (3·2%) of 1355 participants receiving insulin glargine; all deaths except one (in the insulin glargine group) were deemed unrelated to treatment.
sections.conclusion: In people with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk, the cardiovascular safety of orforglipron was confirmed by demonstrating non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most frequent adverse event and most common reason for orforglipron treatment discontinuation with orforglipron, while clinically significant hypoglycaemia occurred less frequently with orforglipron than with insulin glargine. These findings support orforglipron as a potential once-daily, oral treatment option with established cardiovascular safety in people with type 2 diabetes and increased cardiovascular risk.

picks.title: Efficacy and safety of garetosmab, an activin A-blocking antibody, in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (OPTIMA): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) is an ultrarare genetic disorder resulting in progressive heterotopic ossification of ligaments, tendons, and muscles, leading to disability and early mortality. FOP is caused by heterozygous gain-of-function mutations in the activin receptor type 1A, allowing this receptor to be aberrantly activated by activin A (ActA), which normally inhibits this receptor, thus driving heterotopic bone formation. In preclinical models and an earlier phase 2 trial (LUMINA-1) in FOP, an antibody blocking ActA (garetosmab) prevented heterotopic ossification. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of garetosmab in adults living with FOP.
sections.methods: OPTIMA is a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial conducted at 18 study sites across 16 countries and regions. Participants aged 18 years or older with FOP were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to monthly intravenous placebo, garetosmab 3 mg/kg, or garetosmab 10 mg/kg. Randomisation was stratified by baseline Cumulative Analogue Joint Involvement Scale score and previous participation in the LUMINA-1 study. The primary efficacy and safety endpoints were total number of new heterotopic bone lesions at week 56 and treatment-emergent adverse events of special interest (AESIs) through week 56, analysed in all randomised participants who received at least one dose of the study drug. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05394116); the trial is active (completed primary endpoint) but not recruiting participants.
sections.results: Between Nov 21, 2022, and July 4, 2024, 63 participants were enrolled and randomly assigned (placebo, n=21; garetosmab 3 mg/kg, n=19; garetosmab 10 mg/kg, n=23). The mean age was 26·6 years (SD 6·8); 38 (60%) participants were female and 25 (40%) male. 62 participants completed 56 weeks of treatment; one participant in the placebo group discontinued at 53 weeks. The total number of new heterotopic bone lesions was significantly lower with garetosmab: there were 19 lesions with placebo versus one lesion with garetosmab 3 mg/kg (rate ratio vs placebo: 0·06 [95% CI 0·00-0·73]; p=0·027) and two lesions with garetosmab 10 mg/kg (rate ratio vs placebo: 0·10 [0·01-0·76]; p=0·026). Treatment-emergent AESIs occurred in one (5%) of 21 participants receiving placebo, zero of 19 receiving garetosmab 3 mg/kg, and four (17%) of 23 receiving garetosmab 10 mg/kg; all were considered treatment-related. No deaths occurred.
sections.conclusion: Garetosmab substantially reduced the number of new heterotopic bone lesions, providing robust evidence of its potential to be an efficacious and generally well tolerated disease-modifying therapy for FOP.

picks.title: The pyrin inflammasome senses OCTN2-mediated uptake of extracellular ʟ-carnitine from muscle injury or ingestion.
picks.abstract: Red-meat-containing diets are epidemiologically associated with diseases of chronic inflammation, while diets that restrict red meat improve health. Yet, it is uncertain how red meat incites inflammation. Here, we discover that ʟ-carnitine, an amino acid highly concentrated in skeletal muscle myocytes, drives inflammasome activation in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-challenged mice and LPS-primed murine and human macrophages. We find that extracellular ʟ-carnitine represses mevalonate synthesis, thereby triggering activation of the pyrin inflammasome, downstream of cellular import by the high-affinity ʟ-carnitine transporter OCTN2. We find that the inflammatory response to skeletal muscle injury also requires pyrin and OCTN2. Thus, in summary, we identify macrophages as sentinels of exogenous and endogenous extracellular ʟ-carnitine that serve as a proxy for skeletal myocyte damage, and we open the field to examine the mechanistic basis for how excess dietary intake of carnitine-rich food drives inflammatory disease.

picks.title: Frequency encoding regulates cell type composition in the small intestine.
picks.abstract: Intestinal homeostasis requires tight regulation of stem cell maintenance and differentiation to absorptive and secretory cell types, two major intestinal lineages. Key signaling pathways have been identified, but how they balance cell type composition remains unclear. We uncovered oscillatory expression of the Notch-target protein Hes1 (hairy and enhancer of split 1) that controls cell fate specification in a frequency-dependent manner. An endogenous fluorescent Hes1 reporter revealed distinct, cell type-specific oscillation frequencies forming a gradient along the crypt-villus axis, which was modulated by cell cycle phase as well as Wnt (wingless-related integration site)-signaling and Notch-signaling activity. We developed a microfluidic system to modulate Notch-signaling oscillations in organoids and found the oscillation frequency to regulate the balance of cell type composition. This study provides evidence that information for cell fate specification is encoded in the frequency of an oscillatory signal.

items.title: Prostatic Artery Embolization in a Patient With Bilateral Internal Iliac Artery Occlusions.
items.abstract: Background: Prostatic artery embolization (PAE) is an established treatment for lower urinary tract symptoms due to benign prostatic hyperplasia but can be challenging in complex anatomy. Study Sample: An 86-year-old male with history of abdominal aortic aneurysm repair and aortobifemoral bypass presented with gross hematuria and urinary retention. Imaging and clinical evaluation confirmed BPH-related clot retention as the etiology. Careful review of preprocedural CT angiography revealed occluded bilateral internal iliac arteries, a right aberrant obturator artery (AOA) (corona mortis variant), arising from the inferior epigastric artery, which itself originated from the native right external iliac artery. The AOA supplied the entire prostate, perfusing both lobes and contributing to the contralateral pelvic circulation as well. Cone-beam CT and angiography confirmed the perfusion to both prostatic lobes. PAE was performed by accessing the native common femoral artery and selectively catheterizing the AOA. Embolization of the prostatic parenchyma was completed successfully while preserving flow to adjacent pelvic structures, avoiding non-target embolization. Results: The patient had complete resolution of hematuria and urinary retention and remained catheter-free at 1-year follow-up. Conclusions: This case highlights the importance of pre-procedural evaluation and planning, demonstrating that PAE can be safely and effectively performed even in variant vascular anatomy.

items.title: Symptomatic Superior Vena Cava Lipoma Causing Near-Complete Venous Obstruction: A Case Report and Literature Review.
items.abstract: BackgroundLipomas are common benign mesenchymal tumors; however, intravascular localization is exceedingly rare. Superior vena cava (SVC) involvement represents an exceptional entity, with only a limited number of cases reported in the literature. Intravascular lipomas are frequently detected incidentally but may present with symptoms related to venous obstruction, including superior vena cava syndrome. We report a rare case of SVC-origin intravascular lipoma extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, accompanied by a focused review of previously published upper extremity cases.Case PresentationA 77-year-old male presented with facial and cervical edema, dyspnea exacerbated in the supine position, and distended cervical veins. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a 5-cm elongated, fat-attenuation mass within the SVC extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, causing near-total (approximately 99%) luminal occlusion. Transthoracic echocardiography supported the diagnosis. The patient underwent surgical resection via median sternotomy under cardiopulmonary bypass. Following longitudinal venotomy of the SVC extending to the brachiocephalic vein, the tumor-adherent to the posterior venous wall-was completely excised with preservation of vascular integrity. Primary venous repair was performed. The diagnosis of lipoma was histopathologically confirmed. The patient initially showed marked symptomatic improvement; however, on postoperative day 5, sudden-onset dyspnea necessitated reintubation, followed by multiorgan failure and death. The precise cause of the acute deterioration could not be definitively established.Literature review identified only 21 previously reported upper extremity intravenous lipomas, with this case representing the 16th involving the SVC and the oldest reported patient.ConclusionUpper extremity intravenous lipomas are rare and may lead to significant venous obstruction. Cross-sectional imaging is essential for diagnosis and surgical planning. In symptomatic patients, complete surgical excision provides definitive treatment and symptom relief. Management of incidentally detected asymptomatic cases remains controversial and should be individualized.

items.title: Intravascular Lithotripsy of Aortic and Renal Lesions as a Therapeutic Tool for Pickering Syndrome: A Case Report.
items.abstract: We report the case of a 73-year-old woman admitted with Pickering syndrome, a life-threatening condition characterized by recurrent flash pulmonary edema secondary to severe renovascular disease. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated an atrophic left kidney, a heavily calcified visceral aorta with a coral-reef morphology, and a near-occlusive stenosis of the right renal artery. Urgent endovascular treatment was performed with intravascular lithotripsy for plaque modification of the suprarenal aorta and the right renal artery, followed by renal artery stenting. The patient showed prompt clinical recovery, with resolution of pulmonary edema, stabilization of blood pressure, and improvement of renal function. This case illustrates the potential role of intravascular lithotripsy as a minimally invasive adjunct for managing severely calcified aorto-renal disease in high-risk patients, enabling endovascular treatment in otherwise challenging anatomy.

items.title: Transarterial Computed Tomographic Angiography in Patients With Impaired Renal Function Undergoing Endovascular Aortic Repair.
items.abstract: PurposeComputed tomography angiography (CTA) is crucial for preoperative planning and postoperative surveillance of endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). Renal function impairment however limits pre- and postoperative assessment. The aim of our study was to evaluate the safety and diagnostic value of a novel technique in the setting of patients undergoing EVAR.Methods216 patients with chronic kidney disease undergoing transbrachial placement of an angiography catheter in the aorta for contrast medium administration were analyzed retrospectively. 45 patients with normal kidney function and aortic aneurysms were included as control group. 27 were female, 84 cases were for thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm, while 106 cases were for abdominal aortic aneurysm. Primary endpoint was the freedom from contrast-induced acute kidney injury. Secondary safety endpoints were freedom from access site complications and cerebrovascular incidents. Imaging quality endpoints were attenuation values and contrast-to-noise-ratios in predefined vessels, validated by intraclass correlation coefficients.ResultsMean creatinine change was -.11 mg/dL, mean GFR change was 2.13% in the intervention group. There were 10 (4.6%) false aneurysms and two access site hematoma (0.93%). Two cerebrovascular incidents (0.9%) were transient. Transarterial CTA attenuation values varied between 210.4 (±89) and 241.4 (±98) Hounsfield units (HU), and 306.35 (±63.27) to 321.39 (±70.12) HU in the control group. The mean amount of contrast medium used in the catheter group was significantly reduced (31.70 ± 5.82 mL) compared to the control group (P = .001). Contrast-to-noise ratios varied between 9.1 (±4.6) and 11.1 (±4.4. Intraclass correlation coefficients between the readings were very good (0.987-0.992).ConclusionCatheter-based transarterial computed tomographic angiography is a safe and efficacious way to evaluate patients with aortic aneurysms, both prior and after EVAR.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of QY201, an oral dual Janus kinase 1/tyrosine kinase 2 inhibitor, in adults with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis: a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 dose-finding trial.

sections.objective: QY201 is a novel oral Janus kinase 1 and tyrosine kinase 2 inhibitor. To evaluate the efficacy of multiple QY201 doses in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (AD), and to inform dose selection for phase 3 studies.
sections.methods: In this phase 2, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 200 adults with moderate-to-severe AD were randomized 1:1:1:1 to receive QY201 (5 mg, 10 mg, or 20 mg twice daily [BID]) or placebo for 12 weeks. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving ≥75% improvement in Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI-75) at week 12.
sections.results: EASI-75 response rates at week 12 were 72.9%, 84.7% and 81.4% in the 5 mg BID, 10 mg BID, and 20 mg BID groups, respectively, compared with 18.5% in the placebo group (all P<0.0001). Investigator's Global Assessment response rates were 44.7% (P=0.0011), 64.3% (P<0.0001), and 71.3% (P<0.0001), respectively, versus 12.4% with placebo. Treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 74.0%, 75.5%, and 90.4% of patients receiving QY201, compared to 69.4% with placebo; most were mild or moderate.
sections.conclusion: The phase 2 findings support further evaluation of QY201 at doses of 10 mg BID and 20 mg BID in confirmatory phase 3 trials.
sections.other: Short follow-up and single-country population.

items.title: Dyspnea during resting breathing and carbon dioxide rebreathing in adult patients with congenital central hypoventilation syndrome.

sections.objective: Congenital central hypoventilation syndrome (CCHS) is an ultra-rare genetic disorder caused by PHOX2B mutations. Patients lack central CO2 chemosensitivity and require ventilatory support during sleep. Children with CCHS have been reported to lack CO2-induced air hunger, but respiratory sensations and dyspnea have not been characterized in adults.
sections.methods: This was a prospective controlled observational study conducted on a convenience sample derived from a national cohort of an ultrarare disease. Thirteen adult CCHS patients carrying PHOX2B mutations underwent Multidimensional Dyspnea Profile (MDP) assessment during unassisted resting breathing and at the end of CO2 rebreathing. Healthy controls were studied under the same conditions.
sections.results: Before the study, none of the patients had spontaneously reported dyspnea or bothersome respiratory sensations. When prompted with the MDP during resting breathing, 9/13 patients described breathing unpleasantness (non-zero MDP-A1) versus 0/18 controls (p < 0.0001), and 12/13 fulfilled criteria for dyspnea defined as breathing awareness associated with negative affect. During CO2 rebreathing, ventilatory responses remained profoundly blunted, yet breathing unpleasantness increased. Compared with controls, patients had lower sensory and affective ratings, with less frequent air hunger (p = 0.0108). MDP ratings did not correlate with ventilatory response to CO2 or genotype.
sections.conclusion: Adult CCHS patients can experience conscious unpleasant breathing awareness at rest and retain a perceptual response to CO2 despite abolished or nearly abolished central chemosensitivity. These findings suggest respiratory interoceptive pathways beyond canonical brainstem chemosensitive circuits and support active multidimensional assessment of dyspnea in adult CCHS patients.
sections.other: Do genetically characterized adult CCHS patients experience respiratory sensations and dyspnea during unassisted resting breathing and CO2 rebreathing, and along which dimensions?

items.title: Peritoneal dialysis induces hepatic metabolic stress as an instigator for systemic inflammation.

sections.objective: Peritoneal dialysis (PD) is a lifesaving therapy in patients with kidney failure, but results in daily intraperitoneal glucose administration corresponding to 50% of the recommended energy intake, most of which enters the portal circulation. As the impact of this glucose exposure on liver and metabolic health remains unclear, we explored hepatic and systemic metabolic effects of PD.
sections.methods: Healthy mice and mice with chronic kidney disease (5/6 nephrectomy C57BL/6 aged 12-14 weeks) underwent seven weeks of PD. Combining morphologic studies, untargeted tissue proteomics, targeted plasma metabolomics and spatial transcriptomics, we assessed hepatic molecular and metabolic effects of PD. Gut- and gut-vascular barriers, systemic and hepatic lipopolysaccharide abundance and zonal transcriptional changes were assessed with multiplexed spatial single-cell analysis and transcriptomics.
sections.results: Intraperitoneally administered glucose during PD was rapidly taken up by the liver and induced hepatic metabolic inflammation. Portal-venous glucose overload bypassing the gastrointestinal tract resulted in increased glucose-to-cholesterol shunting with elevated plasma cholesterol levels, despite the absence of hepatic steatosis or glycogen storage. Increased oxidative stress and endotoxin load were associated with reduced hepatic Kupffer cell numbers without increased gut permeability.
sections.conclusion: Ours study found chronic hepatic metabolic stress induced by PD. Evidence of hepatic glucotoxicity and oxidative stress as instigators for systemic metabolic inflammation induced by PD suggests that similar pathologic mechanisms could also contribute to increased cardiometabolic risk on chronic PD.

items.title: Safety outcomes of semaglutide by chronic kidney disease severity in the FLOW trial.

sections.objective: People with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) often experience medication intolerance and side effects that worsen with lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). This prespecified secondary analysis assessed the safety of semaglutide by baseline eGFR.
sections.methods: FLOW (NCT03819153) was a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial testing the efficacy of subcutaneous semaglutide 1.0 mg once-weekly on a primary kidney outcome (50% or more eGFR reduction, kidney failure, or death due to kidney or cardiovascular causes) in participants with T2D and CKD. Safety data were collected selectively and included serious adverse events (SAEs), AEs leading to treatment discontinuation, and prespecified AEs of special interest (AESIs). In this descriptive assessment, systematically collected safety data were reported numerically by baseline eGFR.
sections.results: Of 3533 participants, 1767 received semaglutide and 1766 received placebo. Fewer SAEs were reported with semaglutide than placebo across baseline eGFR subgroups (45.1% versus 50.4% in the 60 or more ml/min per 1.73 m2 subgroup, and 56.4% versus 60.4% in the under 30 ml/min per 1.73 m2 subgroup). SAEs related to infections and infestations; cardiac disorders; respiratory, thoracic and mediastinal disorders; and metabolism and nutrition disorders were generally less frequent with semaglutide than placebo, regardless of baseline eGFR. Treatment discontinuations due to AEs were higher with lower baseline eGFR across treatment groups (60 or more ml/min per 1.73 m2: semaglutide 11.2%, placebo 11.3%; under30 ml/min per 66 1.73 m2: semaglutide 18.8%, placebo 18.7%). Discontinuations specifically due to gastrointestinal AEs were reported more frequently with semaglutide (4.5%) than placebo (1.1%), regardless of baseline eGFR. Frequencies of AESI were similar between treatment groups across baseline eGFR subgroups.
sections.conclusion: In this safety assessment, SAEs were reported less frequently with semaglutide than placebo, with corresponding patterns observed for treatment discontinuations and AESIs. No unexpected safety concerns were identified across the spectrum of eGFR represented in the FLOW trial.

items.title: A study using the REIN registry suggests a statin therapy benefits for secondary prevention in patients receiving dialysis.

sections.objective: While statins are effective for cardiovascular prevention in the general population, their benefit in patients with CKD G5D (kidney failure treated by dialysis) remains uncertain. Previous randomized controlled trials included mixed populations for primary and secondary prevention while excluding patients with recent cardiovascular events, leaving a knowledge gap regarding statin effectiveness for secondary prevention immediately following an atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) event. Here, we address this gap by providing real-world evidence.
sections.methods: We conducted a landmark-based observational study, informed by the target trial framework using the French Renal Epidemiology and Information Network (REIN) registry and merged with data from the French national healthcare system database from 2010 to 2023. We included adults with CKD G5D who experienced an ASCVD event. We used inverse probability of treatment weighting to balance baseline characteristics between statin initiators and non-initiators, thereby estimating the average causal effect on all-cause mortality. Results focus on the relative and absolute risk difference and the life expectancy gain using delta restricted mean survival time (dRMST).
sections.results: The study cohort included 5534 patients (median age: 75 years; 67% male). During the ten years of follow-up, statin use was associated with a reduced risk of mortality. The survival curves reached a maximum absolute difference at year four (risk difference -6.2% (95% CI: -10.2; -2.2); relative risk 0.88 [95% CI: 0.81; 0.96]). Life expectancy extended significantly over time with a mean survival gain of 69 days at five years (95% CI: 14-125) and reaching 135 days at ten years (95% CI: 31-239). No difference was identified between groups regarding hospitalizations for rhabdomyolysis or toxic hepatitis.
sections.conclusion: In patients receiving dialysis, statin initiation following an ASCVD event is safe and associated with a modest-to-moderate ten-year cumulative survival benefit. While interpreted within observational limitations, this real-world evidence supports their use in this secondary prevention setting.

items.title: The Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) study measured hepcidin, cardiovascular, kidney and metabolic outcomes in chronic kidney disease.

sections.objective: Abnormal iron homeostasis plays a critical role in extra-hematopoietic disorders. The relationship of hepcidin, the master iron regulator, to clinical outcomes, has not been characterized in a large cohort of chronic kidney disease (CKD).
sections.methods: To determine if plasma hepcidin level predicts cardiovascular (CV), kidney, and metabolic outcomes in patients with CKD, we studied 3826 patients enrolled in the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) study. Hazard ratios for hepcidin tertiles were estimated from Cox Proportional Hazards regression for primary outcomes of incident heart failure (HF), end stage kidney disease (kidney failure) or halving of the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and new onset diabetes or prediabetes. Secondary outcomes included atherosclerotic events and all-cause and CV mortality.
sections.results: The median and interquartile range of plasma hepcidin level was 43 (22, 77) ng/mL. Higher plasma hepcidin levels were associated with older age, male sex, non-Hispanic Black race, diabetes, lower eGFR, higher albuminuria, increased plasma levels of iron indices, C-terminal fibroblast growth factor 23, and markers of inflammation (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein and interleukin-6). We found no association between plasma hepcidin level and the risk for incident HF or prediabetes/diabetes. However, compared to the middle tertile, the highest hepcidin tertile was independently associated with increased risk for kidney outcomes (hazard ratio 1.19; 95% confidence interval 1.09, 1.30) and atherosclerotic events (hazard ratio 1.34; 95% confidence interval 1.09, 1.64), while the lowest hepcidin tertile was associated with increased risk for all-cause and CV mortality in fully adjusted multivariable models including iron indices and inflammation.
sections.conclusion: Both low and high plasma levels of hepcidin are associated with adverse clinical outcomes.

items.title: Oxidative Stress Potentiates a STAT1-APOL1 Feedforward Loop and Governs Disease Severity in APOL1-Mediated Kidney Disease.

sections.objective: Apolipoprotein L1 (APOL1) risk variants (G1 and G2) confer immunity against Trypanosoma infection but markedly increase susceptibility to progressive kidney disease. However, only a subset of biallelic risk-variant carriers develops disease progression, distinct from murine models. Here, we evaluated molecular drivers of progressive kidney disease using a model that reflected the low human disease penetrance.
sections.methods: To investigate the heterogeneity of APOL1-mediated kidney disease, we generated novel APOL1 bacterial artificial chromosome transgenic mice with doxycycline-inducible systemic interferon-γ expression (G0- or G1-IFNγ mice). Podocyte-specific transcriptomics using translating ribosome affinity purification (TRAP-seq) and single-cell spatial transcriptomics via 10x Genomics Xenium In Situ platform was performed. Mechanistic validation and analysis of factors regulating APOL1 upregulation were conducted in primary podocytes and subsequently validated in mouse kidney and in human kidney biopsy specimens via immunofluorescence.
sections.results: A subset of G1-IFNγ mice developed severe albuminuria and focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, which strongly correlated with the magnitude of APOL1 upregulation. By pairing TRAP-seq with single-cell spatial transcriptomic data, we identified mitochondrial dysfunction and JAK-STAT signaling as a central mediator of podocyte injury. In primary podocytes, APOL1 risk variants triggered mitochondrial-derived oxidative stress, establishing a self-amplifying STAT1-APOL1 feedforward loop that further enhances APOL1 expression and APOL1 oligomerization. This pathogenic loop was consistently enriched in podocytes from both G1-IFNγ mice and in kidney biopsy specimens from patients with APOL1-mediated focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, demonstrating translational relevance.
sections.conclusion: Our findings suggest that biallelic risk variants initiate an oxidative stress-induced positive feedforward loop which promotes and sustains APOL1 upregulation and STAT1 phosphorylation, thereby contributing to disease susceptibility, severity and outcome.

items.title: Mastering the Eye: Clinical Paradigm Shifts from Optical Restoration to Genomic Correction.
items.abstract: Historically, the main operation for cataract was couching, and the interior of the living eye could not be examined until Hermann von Helmholtz introduced the ophthalmoscope in 1851. Since the mid-twentieth century, seven advances have reshaped ophthalmic care. Harold Ridley implanted the first intraocular lens in 1949, and the ophthalmologist Charles Kelman and the engineer Anton Banko developed phacoemulsification, reported in 1967. Robert Machemer performed the first pars plana vitrectomy in 1970, while David Huang and colleagues described optical coherence tomography in 1991. Endothelial keratoplasty, developed by Gerrit Melles and others between 1998 and 2006, replaced only the failing corneal endothelium instead of the full thickness of the cornea. Anti-VEGF therapy followed the purification of VEGF by Napoleone Ferrara and colleagues in 1989 and the approval of ranibizumab in 2006. Minimally invasive glaucoma surgery has spread since 2012, and in 2017 voretigene neparvovec became the first approved gene therapy for an inherited retinal disease. Five of these advances enabled a new type of intervention, whereas endothelial keratoplasty and minimally invasive glaucoma surgery made existing operations safer. For each advance we summarize the best available evidence of benefit to patients and its certainty, which is high for some, such as anti-VEGF therapy, and low for others, such as the effect of imaging on patient outcomes. Each advance created new burdens, from chronic injections to dependence on donor tissue, and routine adoption depended on manufacturing, regulation, cost, reimbursement, and health-system capacity.

items.title: Early and follow-up results of reinterventions for type 2 endoleak following endovascular repair of abdominal aortic aneurysm (EVAR): the multicenter REinterventions for Type 2 Endoleak (RETE) study.

sections.objective: Type II endoleak (T2EL) is frequent after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) and may require reintervention in selected patients. However, the optimal treatment strategy for durable resolution remains uncertain. The aim of this study is to retrospectively analyze perioperative and long-term results of T2Els' reinterventions, both endovascular and open surgical, in a large patient cohort from twenty high-volume academic centers.
sections.methods: A retrospective analysis of consecutive patients undergoing first reintervention for T2ELs was conducted across 20 centers over a 10-year period. Patients requiring concomitant treatment for other endoleak types were excluded. A total of 403 patients were included. Primary outcomes included technical success, 30-day AAA-related mortality and reintervention-free survival during follow-up. Secondary outcomes were perioperative complications, early reintervention, overall survival, freedom from aneurysm-related death and rupture, freedom from recurrent endoleaks, freedom from open conversion or semi-conversion in patients previously treated endovascularly and sac behavior during follow-up. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression analyses were performed to analyze follow-up results.
sections.results: Patients were predominantly male (90%) with a mean age of 77 years. Reintervention was indicated for sac enlargement in 94.5% of cases; 4% presented with rupture. Median time from EVAR to reintervention was 4.3 years. Lumbar arteries (55%) and the inferior mesenteric artery (35%) were the main sources. Endovascular treatment was performed in 86% and open conversion/semi-conversion in 14%. Technical success was 96%, with 1% mortality and 4% major complications. Overall survival was 80.5% and rupture-free survival 79.2% at 5 years. Recurrent T2EL occurred in 64.2%, and reintervention-free survival was 48.3%. Endovascular group showed significantly lower freedom from reintervention rates when compared to open conversion/semi conversion group (42.4% vs 86.8%, SE 0.04 vs SE 0.05, p<0.001, log-rank 15.9). Conversion/semi-conversion after endovascular treatment occurred in 14%. No differences were recorded comparing different fabric materials of the endograft in terms of freedom for reintervention and freedom from open surgery. A sac diameter ≥7 cm at the time of reintervention predicted further reinterventions, while primary open treatment improved durability.
sections.conclusion: Reinterventions for T2ELs are safe, with satisfactory immediate technical success and low perioperative mortality. During follow-up, risks of rupture and AAA-related death remain low. However, the endoleak recurrence rate exceeds 60% at five years, necessitating reintervention in over 40% of patients. Early intervention for patients with a sac diameter approaching 7 cm can be suggested, while a primary open approach may be considered in low-risk patients.

items.title: More than just accuracy: A pathway-level framework for implementing blood and digital biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease care.
items.abstract: Blood biomarkers are transforming Alzheimer's disease diagnostics by enabling a scalable, minimally invasive assessment of pathology. Food and Drug Administration clearances and European market certifications of different plasma tests mark a shift toward biological diagnosis in routine care. However, clinical implementation is not guided by diagnostic accuracy alone but will depend on improved patient-centered and pathway-level outcomes, including diagnostic confidence, the appropriate use of CSF and PET assessments, time to diagnosis, amyloid-targeting treatment eligibility assessment, and trial recruitment. Digital biomarkers may complement blood tests by providing repeated measures of cognition, speech, and mobility. Yet, their evidence base remains more heterogeneous regarding construct validity, supervision requirements, device dependence, adherence burden, cultural portability, interpretability, and regulatory classification. This review defines how combined blood-digital workflows could be evaluated beyond accuracy, including the context of use, downstream decisions, ethical aspects, governance, and post-market monitoring, ultimately aiming to translate biomarker innovation into meaningful benefits for patients and health systems.

items.title: Joint American Academy of Dermatology-Hidradenitis Suppurativa Foundation guidelines of care for the management of hidradenitis suppurativa.

sections.objective: Hidradenitis suppurativa affects 0.7% to 1.5% of the global population and causes substantial disability and meaningfully impairs quality of life. To provide evidence-based recommendations for the management of hidradenitis suppurativa.
sections.methods: A workgroup conducted a systematic review and applied the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach to assess the certainty of evidence and to develop recommendations.
sections.results: This guideline presents 37 evidence-based recommendations. Strong recommendations are made for adalimumab, bimekizumab, infliximab, secukinumab, and routine pain assessment. Conditional recommendations are made for topical clindamycin, resorcinol, and ruxolitinib; oral doxycycline, tetracycline, and clindamycin with rifampin; intravenous ertapenem; spironolactone; short-term systemic corticosteroids; upadacitinib; specific procedural interventions; tobacco cessation; supportive pain management; and zinc supplementation and vitamin D repletion.
sections.conclusion: These guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations for the management of hidradenitis suppurativa.
sections.other: Analysis is limited to best evidence available from systematic review.

items.title: Percutaneous and Endovascular Embolization-Based Treatments of Type 1A and Type 1B Endoleaks after Endovascular Aneurysm Repair.
items.abstract: ObjectiveThis retrospective, observational study was conducted to evaluate the efficacy of embolization-based treatments for Types 1A and 1B endoleaks following endovascular aneurysm repair.DesignA total of 26 patients who underwent endovascular aneurysm repair between January 2005 and September 2023 and subsequently received embolization therapy for Types 1A or 1B endoleak, either at the end of the procedure or during follow-up, were retrospectively reviewed.MethodsEmbolization was performed in 16 patients with Type 1A endoleaks and 10 with Type 1B. Eight of the 16 patients who underwent embolization for Type 1A endoleaks required additional treatments such as aortic cuff placement or a chimney graft. Similarly, six out of the 10 patients treated with embolization for Type 1B endoleaks underwent adjunctive procedures such as iliac stent-graft extension. The primary endpoint was the absence of aneurysm sac enlargement. Secondary endpoints included technical success and the avoidance of endoleak-related reintervention.ResultsAneurysm sac regression or stabilization was observed in 68.7% of Type 1A and 70% of Type 1B endoleak cases over mean follow-up periods of 43.1 and 22.3 months, respectively.ConclusionEmbolization-based endovascular treatment, alone or combined with adjunctive endograft procedures, may achieve aneurysm sac stabilization or regression in a substantial proportion of patients with Types 1A and 1B endoleaks. However, the possibility of recurrence and reintervention, particularly in Type 1A endoleaks, remains an important limitation of this approach and warrants continued imaging surveillance.

items.title: Multimodal KCNQ1 Variant-Effect Maps Define Ion Channel Mechanisms and Disease Risk.

sections.objective: Variants in the ion channel gene KCNQ1 are the leading cause of congenital long QT syndrome (LQTS), a disorder characterized by QT prolongation and risk of fatal arrhythmias. The expanding use of genetic testing has led to the identification of numerous variants of uncertain significance, complicating clinical interpretation and risk stratification. Functional characterization of KCNQ1 variants is essential to define their role in long QT syndrome and advance precision medicine in cardiovascular care.
sections.methods: We generated a nearly comprehensive variant library of 13 403 protein-coding variants in KCNQ1. Using 4 pooled assays followed by high-throughput sequencing, we characterized the variants' effects on cell surface abundance and channel function in both the variant-only and heterozygous states. Case-control analyses and data from large-scale biobanks were used to assess the clinical impact of loss-of-function variants on QT prolongation and long QT syndrome. Heterozygous assay results were used to determine dominant-negative effects, which were also evaluated for association with arrhythmia risk. Protein structural clustering of distinct classes of deleterious variants was analyzed.
sections.results: Across the 4 assays, we generated 49 305 functional measurements of KCNQ1 variants. Of the 13 403 KCNQ1 studied variants, 1757 demonstrated strong pathogenic evidence, and 6660 showed moderate benign evidence. Loss-of-function variants were significantly associated with QT prolongation and long QT syndrome in case-control and biobank analyses. Deleterious variants clustered within distinct structural domains based on their functional classification. A majority of pathogenic variants exhibited dominant-negative effects; these variants were linked to a higher risk of arrhythmia diagnoses than were haploinsufficient variants.
sections.conclusion: This comprehensive KCNQ1 functional atlas provides novel functional evidence for most KCNQ1 variants of uncertain significance. It also reveals mechanistic principles linking genetic variation to ion channel biology and arrhythmia susceptibility, advancing cardiovascular precision medicine.

items.title: Prognostic Value of Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve From a Large Nationwide Cohort.

sections.objective: The diagnostic value of coronary computed tomography angiography-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR-CT) in stable coronary artery disease is well established. The prognostic value of predicting future cardiovascular events is less clear, as studies are limited by small populations, variable measurement points, composite outcomes, and short follow-up. A nationwide cohort of coronary computed tomography angiography with 3-year follow-up was used to examine the association between FFR-CT measurements and future cardiovascular events.
sections.methods: Patients receiving coronary computed tomography angiography and clinically indicated FFR-CT analysis (HeartFlow) for stable coronary artery disease between 2017 and 2020 at 27 sites across England were included. Lowest per-patient stenosis-specific and distal vessel FFR-CT measurements were related to individual outcomes of myocardial infarction (MI), cardiovascular mortality, all-cause mortality, and revascularization. FFR-CT measurements were divided into subgroups to investigate for a gradient of risk: normal FFR-CT (>0.8), borderline (0.71-0.8), reduced (0.51-0.7), and severely reduced (≤0.5).
sections.results: In total, 7836 patients aged 63 (56.0-71.0), 37.4% women, underwent FFR-CT analysis. Stenosis-specific FFR-CT was associated with future MI (hazard ratio [HR], 2.08-5.73; P<0.001), cardiovascular death (HR, 1.51-3.40; P<0.001), all-cause death (HR, 1.01-1.58; P=0.01), and revascularization (HR, 4.79-24.48; P<0.001), with lower FFR-CT values associated with incrementally greater risk. After adjusting for cardiovascular risk factors and coronary stenosis severity (Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System), stenosis-specific FFR-CT≤0.7 was associated with MI (adjusted HR, 2.94-3.39; P<0.001), ≤0.5 with cardiovascular death (adjusted HR, 2.92; P=0.02), all-cause death (adjusted HR, 1.49; P=0.045), and ≤0.8 with revascularization (adjusted HR, 3.02-9.42; P<0.001). The addition of FFR-CT improved discrimination for MI or cardiovascular death compared with a risk factor and stenosis severity model (C index, 0.783; ∆C index, 0.012; P<0.001). An FFR-CT value of 0.67 defined the optimal cutoff for risk of future cardiovascular events. Distal-vessel FFR-CT was associated with outcomes similar to stenosis-specific FFR-CT. Stenosis-specific and distal-vessel FFR-CT discordance was common (36.4%), but when stenosis-specific FFR-CT was normal, event rates were low (1.5% at 3 years for MI or cardiovascular death).
sections.conclusion: FFR-CT is associated with the individual outcomes of MI, cardiovascular death, and all-cause death independent of risk factors and stenosis severity, with lower FFR-CT values associated with worse outcomes. Reduced and severely reduced FFR-CT have the strongest association with future cardiovascular events, with a value of 0.67 defining the optimal risk threshold.

items.title: Women's Kidney Health in Focus: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
items.abstract: Chronic kidney disease is a global epidemic affecting ≈10% of adults worldwide. Women have a higher prevalence of chronic kidney disease than men yet are less likely to progress to kidney failure, to initiate dialysis, or to receive a kidney transplantation, underscoring the influence of biological sex on chronic kidney disease development, progression, treatment response, and outcomes. Women may also respond differently from men to pharmacological therapies, but they remain underrepresented in clinical trials, limiting the evidence base for sex-specific kidney care. Preclinical evidence implicates a role for estrogen receptor signaling in renal physiology and pathophysiology. Women with chronic kidney disease are at increased risk for adverse pregnancy outcomes and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, and pregnancy complications can also increase future chronic kidney disease risk. Menopause and aging accelerate chronic kidney disease progression in women as a result of declining estradiol and shifts in kidney estrogen receptor profiles. Endocrine and metabolic disorders such as polycystic ovary syndrome increase susceptibility to chronic kidney disease. Family planning, prepregnancy counseling, and antenatal care are essential to support reproductive health in women with chronic kidney disease. Because chronic kidney disease and cardiovascular disease are tightly intertwined, chronic kidney disease is also a leading contributor to cardiovascular mortality in women. Advancing precision kidney medicine for women requires equitable access to kidney care, embedding assessment of reproductive health in chronic care, trial design with adequate power that includes both women and men, and mechanistic studies linking reproductive health to long-term cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease development and progression.

items.title: State of Cardiovascular Disease and Stroke in Hispanic/Latino Adults in the United States: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease became the leading cause of death among Hispanic individuals in the United States in 2022. Hispanic adults experience a disproportionate burden of cardiometabolic risk factors, including obesity, diabetes, and dyslipidemia. Hispanic populations are highly heterogeneous, with substantial variations in genetic ancestry and sociocultural influences that shape cardiovascular disease risk and outcomes. The "Hispanic paradox," describing lower cardiovascular disease mortality despite higher risk factor burden, is increasingly recognized as an oversimplification that does not apply uniformly across Hispanic heritage groups, sexes, or disease types. Disaggregated data reveal substantial differences in risk profiles and disease burden among Hispanic heritage groups, emphasizing the limitations of treating this population as a monolithic unit. Recent evidence demonstrates widening disparities in hypertension control, obesity, diabetes, and metabolic diseases among Hispanic populations, threatening this prior mortality advantage. Advancing cardiovascular and equitable health will require developing a deeper understanding of the unique drivers of cardiovascular disease within diverse Hispanic communities, addressing barriers such as language and insurance access, and implementing culturally tailored interventions and policies. This scientific statement summarizes current cardiovascular disease epidemiology in Hispanic populations, emphasizing heritage group variation and social and structural determinants of health, and presents strategies to improve prevention and healthcare delivery. Key priorities for advancing cardiovascular health in Hispanic adults include expanding disaggregated data collection, increasing representation in research, and ensuring equitable implementation of precision medicine approaches, including genomics, multi-omics, and artificial intelligence, while addressing environmental exposures, psychosocial stressors, and policy-related drivers of risk in order to achieve the American Heart Association's 2028 Impact Goals to advancing health and hope for everyone, everywhere.

items.title: Physiological Left Atrial Staging and the Risk of New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.

sections.objective: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is pervasive and an independent driver of stroke and death in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). Despite guideline recommendations for AF surveillance, effective risk stratification remains elusive, and the hemodynamic and functional states of the left atrium (LA) preceding AF onset remain poorly characterized. We aimed to delineate the hemodynamic and functional states of the LA in HCM, derive a novel LA staging system, and evaluate its prognostic performance for new-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF).
sections.methods: This multicenter retrospective study included consecutive HCM patients with normal left ventricular systolic function from January 2007 to February 2024 at 2 academic referral centers. Patients with valvular heart disease or prior AF were excluded. Patients were categorized by combining the presence of elevated LA pressure (hemodynamic load) and LA contractile strain (intrinsic LA function): stage 1 (normal LA pressure and function), stage 2 (relative contractile augmentation for a given LA pressure), stage 3 (loss of relative contractile augmentation despite elevated LA pressure), stage 4 (elevated LA pressure with decreased LA contractile strain), and isolated LA contractile dysfunction. The primary outcome was NOAF. External validation was conducted in an independent HCM cohort.
sections.results: Of 1,856 patients screened, 705 were eligible (mean age 57.6 ± 13.0 years, 30.1% female). During a median follow-up of 7.5 years (Q1-Q3: 3.6-11.0 years), NOAF occurred in 101. The staging system was independently associated with a significant, stepwise increase in the risk of NOAF (adjusted HR: 1.83 per increment; 95% CI: 1.42-2.37; P < 0.001) and conferred incremental predictive value beyond established risk models (CHARGE-AF and HCM-AF). Consistent results were demonstrated in 1-year landmark and competing-risk analyses, as well as in an external validation cohort (n = 425; age 59.7 ± 13.5 years, 33.9% female). Importantly, serial echocardiography performed in 217 patients 4 to 6 years after baseline revealed a predominantly unidirectional evolution of the proposed LA stage, with most patients remaining stable (39.6%) or progressing to higher stages or AF (43.8%).
sections.conclusion: The proposed LA staging framework offers mechanistic insights into how the LA adapts to progressive diastolic dysfunction in HCM. It is associated with a graded risk of NOAF and may help tailor AF surveillance strategies.

items.title: An Updated Evidence Assessment of the Genetic Causes of Dilated Cardiomyopathy.

sections.objective: Evidence of the diverse genetic architecture of dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) continues to emerge and requires reassessment of the clinical relevance of implicated disease genes. Building on the 2019-2020 Clinical Genome Resource evaluation, the DCM gene curation expert panel reconvened in 2024-2025 to conduct a reassessment of genes in DCM.
sections.methods: The Clinical Genome Resource semiquantitative clinical validity classification framework was applied with specifications to DCM to classify genes into categories on the basis of strength of published evidence for a DCM phenotype. Previously curated genes were reassessed, and newly reported gene-disease-mode of inheritance (MOI) relationships, termed "curations," were evaluated.
sections.results: Sixty-eight genes were evaluated, inclusive of 72 unique gene-disease-MOI relationships across 51 previously evaluated and 17 newly assessed genes. Thirty-five curations were classified as high evidence (16 Definitive, 10 Strong, 9 Moderate), increasing by 16 from the prior assessment. Nine newly assessed genes were classified as high evidence: BAG5, FLII, LMOD2, MYLK3, MYZAP, NRAP, PPA2, PPP1R13L, and RPL3L. Twelve genes (11 newly appraised) were rated as high evidence with an autosomal recessive (AR) MOI. Five reevaluated genes from 2019-2020 had clinically significant changes in classification. Except for JPH2, for which curation was modified to separate autosomal dominant and AR MOI curations, clinically significant changes involved upgrades from low- to high-evidence categories (PLEKHM2, PRDM16, TBX20, TNNI3K), demonstrating the robustness of the Clinical Genome Resource gene curation process over time. An additional 29 gene-disease-MOI curations were classified as Limited, including 6 newly evaluated genes and 1 new MOI for a previously evaluated gene, MYBPC3-AR; 4 were classified as No Known Disease Relationship, and remained Disputed. Four previously evaluated genes were curated for both AD and AR MOIs: JPH2 (AD-Strong, AR-Limited), LDB3 (AD-Limited, AR-Strong), MYBPC3 (AD-Limited, AR-Limited), and TNNI3 (AD- and AR- Strong).
sections.conclusion: With substantial new evidence, the genetic architecture of DCM has rapidly expanded. This updated assessment of genes reported in DCM yielded 35 high-evidence curations, an increase from 19 only 5 years ago. The results of this evidence-based evaluation process inform clinical interpretation of genetic information in the care of DCM patients and families.

items.title: HNRNPK Lactylation Amplifies Inflammation and Exacerbates Myocardial Ischemia/Reperfusion Injury by Regulating Jag2 Splicing.

sections.objective: Myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury triggers profound metabolic reprogramming and lactate accumulation. However, how this metabolic stress regulates inflammatory gene expression remains poorly understood. We hypothesized that lactylation, a lactate-derived posttranslational modification, links metabolic stress to aberrant RNA splicing and cardiac inflammation through the RNA-binding protein HNRNPK (heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein K).
sections.methods: We analyzed atrial tissues from patients undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass and murine ischemia/reperfusion hearts to assess lactylation dynamics. Lactylation-specific proteomics, RNA sequencing, and crosslinking and immunoprecipitation followed by quantitative polymerase chain reaction were used to identify HNRNPK targets. Mechanisms were defined using site-directed mutagenesis (HNRNPK-K405R), isoform-specific overexpression, and a therapeutic splice-switching antisense oligonucleotide in mice and cardiomyocytes.
sections.results: Reperfusion significantly increased global protein lactylation in human and murine myocardium. Proteomics identified HNRNPK as a key target, specifically lactylated at lysine 405 (K405la). Ischemia-induced K405la promoted HNRNPK binding to Jag2 pre-mRNA, suppressing exon 10 skipping and shifting splicing from the Jag2 (Jagged2) short (Jag2-S) to the long (Jag2-L) isoform. Jag2-L, but not Jag2-S, exhibited high affinity for Notch1, hyperactivating Notch-NF-κB (nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells) signaling and exacerbating inflammation and infarct size. Mice expressing a lactylation-deficient variant (HNRNPK-K405R) were protected from ischemia/reperfusion injury. Treatment with a specific antisense oligonucleotide (Jag2-i9) that blocks the HNRNPK-Jag2 interaction prevented Jag2-L production and attenuated cardiac dysfunction.
sections.conclusion: HNRNPK lactylation acts as a metabolic sensor coupling lactate accumulation to pathogenic Jag2 splicing. Targeting this metabolic-splicing axis offers a precise therapeutic strategy to limit inflammation and preserve cardiac function in ischemic heart disease.

items.title: Clinical Considerations in Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy in Pregnancy: JACC State-of-the-Art Review.
items.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) in pregnancy presents unique hemodynamic and arrhythmic challenges despite generally low maternal mortality. This JACC State-of-the-Art Review synthesizes current evidence on preconception risk stratification, genetic counseling, antepartum surveillance, arrhythmia management, and delivery and postpartum care. Key considerations include assessing left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, systolic function, and arrhythmia burden and applying CARPREG II (Cardiac Disease in Pregnancy Study II)/modified World Health Organization classifications to guide monitoring intensity. Pregnancy is typically well tolerated in low-risk women, whereas severe obstruction or systolic dysfunction confers high maternal-fetal risk. Multidisciplinary pregnancy heart team management remains essential to optimize outcomes and support informed decision making across the reproductive continuum.

items.title: Natural History of Asymptomatic Phenotypically Mild HCM: Insights From the SHaRe Registry.

sections.objective: Patients with phenotypically mild hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) do not require symptom management, but may be at an earlier stage in the disease course, with potential to benefit from disease-modifying therapies. However, little is known about the natural history and predictors of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Using the Sarcomeric Human Cardiomyopathy Registry, we identified predictors of incident MACE and characterized disease progression in phenotypically mild HCM.
sections.methods: Phenotypically mild HCM was defined as: having shorter disease duration (<10 years since diagnosis or age ≤30 years), no previous MACE, being NYHA functional class I, and having a left ventricular (LV) maximal wall thickness (MWT) <25 mm. These individuals were followed prospectively for the development of symptoms or MACE: atrial fibrillation (AF), malignant ventricular arrhythmia (MVA) (sudden cardiac death, resuscitated arrest, or appropriate defibrillator therapy), heart failure (HF) (cardiac transplantation, LV assist device implantation, LV ejection fraction <35%, or NYHA functional class III or IV symptoms), stroke, or all-cause mortality. Cox regression identified MACE predictors. Linear and latent class mixed models characterized LV remodeling trajectories and risk clusters.
sections.results: Of 2,500 participants with phenotypically mild HCM (mean age 43 years, 31% women) followed for a mean duration of 7 ± 6 years, 534 (21%) developed MACE, including 289 with AF, 69 with MVA, and 193 with HF. Individuals who progressed from NYHA functional class I to ≥ II symptoms during follow-up (n = 585, 23%) were 2.79 times (95% CI: 2.30-3.39 times) more likely to experience MACE. Age at baseline (HR: 1.24; 95% CI: 1.17-1.32 per 10-year increase), body mass index (HR: 1.10; 95% CI: 1.01-1.21 per 5-kg/m2 increase), left atrial (LA) diameter (HR: 1.16; 95% CI: 1.09-1.25 per 5-mm increase), LV MWT (HR: 1.27; 95% CI: 1.10-1.46 per 5-mm increase), and LV outflow tract (LVOT) gradient (HR: 1.08; 95% CI: 1.05-1.12 per 15-mm Hg increase) associated with higher MACE rates. LV late gadolinium enhancement presence was associated with 36% (95% CI: 5%-76%) higher hazard of MACE. Remodeling trajectories during follow-up predicted risk with each 0.5 mm/year steeper increase in LA diameter associating with doubled AF (HR: 2.24; 95% CI: 1.69-2.97) and HF rates (HR: 2.22; 95% CI: 1.62-3.04) and each 0.5 mm/year steeper LV MWT increase associating with doubled MVA rates (HR: 1.92; 95% CI: 1.38-2.69). Higher sustained values and/or steeper increases in LA diameter, LV MWT, or LVOT gradient associated with the highest MACE rates.
sections.conclusion: Approximately 21% of patients with phenotypically mild HCM developed MACE over medium-term follow-up. Older age, symptoms development, and increasing LA diameter, LV hypertrophy, or LVOT gradient associated with MACE, particularly in instances of steeper rate of change. These findings can guide management strategies and inform future studies of disease-modifying therapies.

items.title: Long-Term Outcome of Myectomy Associated With Secondary Mitral Valve Chordal Cutting in Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.

sections.objective: The recent introduction of cardiac myosin inhibitors has modified the therapy of left ventricular outflow obstruction in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and is raising uncertainties regarding the future role of surgery in the management of obstructive HCM. However, it is likely that a proportion of patients will continue to present with advanced, highly symptomatic HCM, despite medical therapy, and require surgical intervention. We previously reported the short-term results of cutting anterior mitral leaflet secondary chordae in combination with septal myectomy in patients with obstructive HCM. This operative approach has shown excellent results in several short-term studies from our and other centers. However, no data are currently available regarding the long-term outcome of this novel surgical procedure. The study sought to investigate the long-term results of myectomy associated with chordal cutting.
sections.methods: Long-term results were assessed in 350 consecutive patients with obstructive HCM who underwent this operation at our center over a 5-year period. Median follow-up was 5.6 years (Q1-Q3: 4.2-6.3 years).
sections.results: Including 2 in-hospital deaths (surgical mortality 0.6%), 6-year overall survival after surgery was 96% and did not differ from that of the general Italian population matched for age and sex (P = 0.331). Follow-up information was available in 344 (99%) patients. At the most recent evaluation, 271 (79%) patients were asymptomatic in NYHA functional class I, 65 (19%) were in NYHA functional class II, and 8 (2%) were in NYHA functional class III. During follow-up, there were 14 deaths, 6 of which were unrelated to HCM. At most recent echocardiographic evaluation, ≥95% of patients had no residual left ventricular outflow gradient, clinically significant mitral regurgitation, or impaired systolic function.
sections.conclusion: Our results show that cutting thickened and/or retracted secondary chordae of the anterior mitral leaflet in association with septal myectomy has excellent long-term clinical and hemodynamic results in patients with obstructive HCM. These findings may further increase the number of myectomy referral centers and the availability of the surgical option for severely symptomatic HCM patients unresponsive to medical treatment.

items.title: Genetic code expansion enables plant-directed control of bacterial activity.
items.abstract: Microorganisms have the potential to deliver growth-promoting benefits to plants and crops; however, to be useful in a field setting, their gene expression should be programmable and restricted to specific plant hosts and conditions. Here, using O-methyl-L-tyrosine (OMY) as a model compound, we establish noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) as a tool for plant-based control of associated microbial activity. We use genetic code expansion to engineer OMY-dependent control of protein synthesis in the soil bacterium Bacillus subtilis. Engineered B. subtilis strains express an orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase and tRNA pair that, upon provision of OMY, results in suppression of in-frame amber stop codons in target transcripts. We engineer Arabidopsis, tomato and poplar to biosynthesize OMY, showing that plant-derived OMY can stimulate gene expression in both model and wild soil bacteria. This demonstrates that inducible and tissue-specific expression of a single biosynthetic enzyme by the plant enables on-demand control over microbial activity, establishing ncAAs as a tool for programming plant-microorganism partnerships.

items.title: The landscape of gene loss and missense variation across the mammalian tree informs on gene essentiality.
items.abstract: Patterns of gene and sequence preservation across species provide insight into gene essentiality under natural selection. Here we developed two interspecies constraint metrics across 462 mammalian species: Gene Identity Score of Mammalian Orthologs (GISMO), which quantifies gene loss weighted by evolutionary distance to humans, and GISMO-mis, which measures missense constraint using the ratio of missense to synonymous variation across mammals. Both metrics are strongly correlated with human loss of function, missense and dosage constraint derived from large-scale sequencing studies, yet are largely independent of coding sequence length. GISMO and GISMO-mis identify essential genes missed by existing human-only metrics, particularly short genes. Genes in the most constrained deciles are enriched for rare variant associations in disorders linked to reduced fecundity, including schizophrenia, autism and neurodevelopmental disorders, and show strong enrichment for common variant heritability. These deciles also exhibit reduced copy number variation, consistent with dosage sensitivity. In addition, GISMO improves prioritization of recessive disease genes and captures signatures of homozygous selection across the mammalian tree. Taken together, GISMO and GISMO-mis leverage deep mammalian evolution to provide complementary, length-robust measures of gene essentiality that strengthen disease-gene prioritization and illuminate the selective forces shaping human biology.

items.title: Dysregulated cholesterol trafficking through ABCA1 drives neurodegeneration in Parkinson's disease.
items.abstract: Although brain cholesterol dysregulation is implicated in Parkinson's disease (PD), targeting cholesterol synthesis has shown limited efficacy. Here we identify ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1) as a critical regulator of cholesterol homeostasis in PD. We show that ABCA1 expression is elevated in the substantia nigra of postmortem PD brains and in a PD mouse model, with regional analyses revealing preferential alterations in nigral and striatal circuits. Mechanistically, astrocytic ABCA1 drives excessive cholesterol efflux in mice, promoting neuronal cholesterol overload. In neurons, ABCA1 localizes to lysosomes, where it facilitates cholesterol import, leading to cholesterol accumulation, autophagy impairment and α-synuclein pathology. Genetic silencing of Abca1 in either astrocytes or dopaminergic neurons attenuates neurodegeneration and behavioral deficits in vivo. Furthermore, we identify magnesium citrate as an ABCA1 inhibitor and show that it reduces dopaminergic neuronal loss in a PD mouse model. Our findings identify an ABCA1-dependent cholesterol pathway underlying PD pathogenesis and support ABCA1 inhibition as a potential disease-modifying strategy.

items.title: Effectiveness of respiratory syncytial virus immunisation in practice.
items.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) affects all ages, with infants and older adults most affected by severe disease. The RSV prevention landscape includes 39 candidates in clinical development, alongside setbacks such as the discontinuation of a promising paediatric live-attenuated vaccine candidate. Several products have been approved, including a maternal vaccine, infant monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines for older adults and adults at high risk. Due to high cost, implementation of these products remains limited to higher-income settings. Real-world evidence confirms high effectiveness, with emerging benefits beyond respiratory disease, including reduced cardiovascular events in older adults. Despite comparable effectiveness of maternal vaccination and monoclonal antibodies, differences in uptake highlight that product availability alone will not ensure population impact. Achieving uptake requires integration into accessible routine care, recommendation by trusted providers, and context-sensitive delivery strategies. This Review summarises RSV preventive products, real-world effectiveness and uptake, and the opportunity of using communication in translating RSV prevention into impact.

items.title: Asymmetric crosstalk between the BMP and TGF-β pathways resolves signaling ambiguity.
items.abstract: The BMP and TGF-β signaling pathways control cellular fate decisions in diverse biological contexts, often playing opposing roles. Despite extensive knowledge of these pathways, understanding how cells respond to environments containing these opposing cues remains a challenge. Here, we systematically analyze the activation of these pathways under combinatorial signaling environments. We find that TGF-β ligands inhibit BMP signaling while BMP ligands enhance TGF-β transcriptional response across concentrations, ligand variants, and cell types.
