This asymmetric crosstalk results in the activation of a TGF-β-biased transcriptional response even under mixed-signaling conditions, effectively reducing signal ambiguity, with implications for processes such as epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). We show that this crosstalk originates downstream of SMAD protein phosphorylation. Using mathematical models, we predict and experimentally verify that promiscuous interactions between SMAD proteins provide the mechanism for the observed crosstalk. Our findings challenge the canonical models, suggesting an active role for mediator proteins in determining biological responses.

items.title: Discovery of phage defense systems through component modularity networks.
items.abstract: Phage defense systems in bacteria exhibit high degrees of modularity, with sensing, signal transmission, and effector enzymes frequently exchanged among phage defense gene clusters. In this study, we capitalize on this modularity to discover phage defense systems by searching for defense-associated modules in new gene contexts across Pseudomonas aeruginosa genomes. This approach reveals a large and interconnected network of modular components distributed across diverse gene clusters. From over 500 candidate defense systems, we select five for experimental testing and validate three: Dionysus, a TerB-encoding system that interferes with early phage infection (EPI) vesicle formation by jumbo phages; Ophion, a radical S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM)-containing system that blocks progression from the EPI vesicle to the nucleus stage during jumbo phage infection; and Hercules, a tightly regulated restriction-modification (RM)-like system. Collectively, we demonstrate that leveraging the modular architecture of phage defense systems is an effective approach to their discovery.

items.title: Time-Varying Spatial Ventricular Gradient Orientation Is Associated With Anthracycline Heart Failure.

sections.objective: Anthracycline use is limited by cardiotoxicity resulting in heart failure (HF). The spatial ventricular gradient (SVG) is a vectorcardiographic measurement of myocardial electrical heterogeneity associated with sudden death and incident HF. It is unclear if serial measurement of SVG after anthracycline initiation can help predict subsequent HF. The objective of the study was to determine if time-varying SVG measurements are associated with anthracycline HF.
sections.methods: Retrospective, single-center study of adult patients with cancer treated with anthracyclines between 1992 to 2019. Standard 12-lead electrocardiograms obtained within 6 months before and up to 5 years after anthracycline initiation were analyzed. Patients with prior HF or ≤1 electrocardiogram within 5 years were excluded. Median vectorcardiograms were constructed, and the SVG vector was obtained by integrating under the X, Y, and Z QRST complexes. Multivariable competing-risks regression was performed with SVG parameters included as time-varying covariates, incident HF as the main outcome, and death as a competing outcome.
sections.results: Among 594 patients (median age 61 years, 48% male), 83 (14%) developed HF within 5 years. In multivariable competing-risks regression, time-varying SVG azimuth (circular angle in the transverse plane) was independently associated with HF (P = 0.0024), demonstrating a 9.4-fold gradient in risk across values. Leftward/anterior azimuth values were the lowest risk areas, whereas posterior/rightward orientations were the highest risk.
sections.conclusion: Time-varying SVG azimuth was independently associated with HF risk in patients treated with anthracyclines. Assessing dynamic changes in SVG azimuth during anthracycline treatment may enhance early identification of patients at risk for HF and inform the use of cardioprotective strategies during cancer therapy.

items.title: METTL4 interacts with histone methylation readers MRG1/2 to regulate alternative splicing and promote thermomorphogenesis in Arabidopsis.
items.abstract: Alternative splicing (AS) functions in thermomorphogenesis, but how AS is regulated during this process remains unclear. Here we show that METTL4 physically interacts with MRG1/2 in Arabidopsis thaliana. The mettl4-1, mrg1 mrg2, and mettl4 mrg1 mrg2 mutants exhibit reduced hypocotyl elongation under warm temperature conditions (28°C), indicating that METTL4 and MRG1/2 cooperatively promote thermomorphogenesis. Transcriptome analysis revealed that both METTL4 and MRG1/2 are required for warm temperature-induced reprogramming of gene transcription and AS. Further analysis showed that METTL4 and MRG1/2 modulate the AS of key brassinosteroid (BR)-signaling genes BES1, GSK1, and SBI1 in thermomorphogenesis. In addition, METTL4 promotes MRG2 binding to the chromatin of BES1 and GSK1 loci. METTL4 also promotes hypocotyl elongation and regulates the AS of BR signaling genes independently of its methyltransferase activity. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that METTL4 and MRG1/2 co-regulate AS and BR signaling to promote thermomorphogenesis in Arabidopsis.

items.title: Engineered human Argonaute 2 for targeted C-to-U RNA base editing.
items.abstract: Tools for manipulating RNA that rely on nonhuman proteins, such as ISC-based and Cas-based scaffolds, can lead to unintended and little-understood effects on human cells and present challenges in therapeutic translation. Replacing them with human proteins engineered for expanded, programmable functions could bypass the limitations of these foreign proteins. Here we demonstrate that human Argonaute 2 (AGO2) can be repurposed as a modular RNA targeting domain. AGO2 fused to a C-to-U deaminase enables AGO-led targeted editing of RNA (ALTER). Using guide RNAs that remodel target RNA structure for selective editing and reduced nuclease activity, we show that ALTER achieves, on average, 1.9-fold higher C-to-U editing on mRNA targets in HEK293T cells compared with Cas13 editors CURE and RESCUE. Transcriptome-wide RNA-seq revealed similar or lower levels of off-target editing compared to the same Cas13-based editors. Machine learning models predict that far fewer immunogenic peptides will result from ALTER and we show that ALTER is amenable to a validated workflow for artificial intelligence-directed deimmunization.

items.title: A systems perspective on monoallelic inborn errors of immunity.
items.abstract: The genetic architecture of inborn errors of immunity continues to grow in complexity, exposing the limitations of variant-centric concepts that have long shaped the field. While complete loss-of-function genotypes have been instrumental in defining essential gene functions in human immunity and inflammation, they have also entrenched binary interpretations of causality that fail to account for pleiotropy, variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance-especially in monoallelic disease. Monoallelic variants often perturb signaling rather than abolishing it. The integration of these perturbations into molecular and cellular systems, and eventually immune circuits, governs phenotypic expression. Here, we revisit and extend classic concepts of genetic dominance and genetic pleiotropy and suggest that these are not sole properties of alleles but emerge from the complex and dynamic behavior of molecular, cellular and immune systems to buffer genetic variance.

items.title: Cortex-wide imaging in naturally behaving mice with 1-gram wireless mesoscopes.
items.abstract: Revealing how distributed cortical circuits coordinate behavior in freely moving animals remains a central challenge in systems neuroscience, constrained by limited fields of view, low throughput, and the tethering required by current miniaturized microscopes1-4. Here, we present Airscope, a wireless mesoscope delivering 4 μm lateral resolution across a 6 mm field of view at 12.5 Hz, weighing 1.0 gram. An aspheric-lens design achieves a 2.84× shorter total track length than previous miniaturized microscopes1,2,5,6 while matching the neuron yield of benchtop one-photon mesoscopes; a tailored wireless link supports cable-free calcium imaging from >8,500 neurons per animal (25‑fold increase). Paired with a zero-shot behavior analyzer, Airscope enables cortical imaging across rich behavioral conditions, including room-scale enriched arenas, swimming assays, and multi-organ implantation, with concurrent recording from multiple animals. Using Airscope, we demonstrate versatile applications of untethered cortical imaging across diverse behavioral paradigms. We identify cortical activity patterns across multiple dorsal regions that correlate with behavioral signatures of social dominance, and show dorsal-cortical population activity prospectively decodes competition outcomes across paired animals. We observe reward-location-associated cortical activity patterns during maze exploration, and characterize Granger-causal influence from spinal cord to cortex during fear conditioning, enabled by simultaneous brain-spinal recordings. By uniting large-scale, cellular-resolution recording with unconstrained behavior, Airscope makes naturalistic, multi-animal cortical recording experimentally practical, and provides a broadly accessible technology for systems neuroscience.

items.title: The pyrin inflammasome senses OCTN2-mediated uptake of extracellular ʟ-carnitine from muscle injury or ingestion.
items.abstract: Red-meat-containing diets are epidemiologically associated with diseases of chronic inflammation, while diets that restrict red meat improve health. Yet, it is uncertain how red meat incites inflammation. Here, we discover that ʟ-carnitine, an amino acid highly concentrated in skeletal muscle myocytes, drives inflammasome activation in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-challenged mice and LPS-primed murine and human macrophages. We find that extracellular ʟ-carnitine represses mevalonate synthesis, thereby triggering activation of the pyrin inflammasome, downstream of cellular import by the high-affinity ʟ-carnitine transporter OCTN2. We find that the inflammatory response to skeletal muscle injury also requires pyrin and OCTN2. Thus, in summary, we identify macrophages as sentinels of exogenous and endogenous extracellular ʟ-carnitine that serve as a proxy for skeletal myocyte damage, and we open the field to examine the mechanistic basis for how excess dietary intake of carnitine-rich food drives inflammatory disease.

items.title: A microbiome-bile acid axis mediates protection from chronic liver disease in females.
items.abstract: Sex-based differences in chronic liver disease (CLD) incidence and progression are well documented, yet the mechanistic basis of this sexual disparity remains elusive. Here, leveraging a large-scale metabolomics database comprising 9,254 individuals, we identify the endogenous bile acid, isoursodeoxycholic acid (isoUDCA), as a candidate mediator of female-associated hepatoprotection. We trace the origin of isoUDCA to a bacterial consortium, which is selectively enriched by estrogen through shaping a specialized intestinal microenvironment. Mechanistically, isoUDCA promotes the nuclear accumulation of SREBP2. This upregulates the intracellular transporter STARD4 and its functionally coupled downstream enzyme CYP7B1, thereby facilitating intracellular cholesterol handling and metabolic conversion. Collectively, our findings support a microbiome-bile acid-liver axis that may contribute to sex differences in CLD susceptibility and support further evaluation of isoUDCA as a potential therapeutic intervention.

items.title: A Study on Renal Artery Variations by CT Angiography and Their Clinical Importance.
items.abstract: AimThis study aimed to evaluate the prevalence, anatomical variations, and branching patterns of the renal arteries using multiphasic computed tomography angiography (CTA), based on the modified classification proposed by Cases et al (2017). Understanding renal artery variations is essential for preoperative planning, renal transplantation, endovascular procedures, and urological interventions.Materials and MethodsA retrospective analysis was conducted on 1220 abdominal CTA studies performed between March 2020 and June 2024. Fourteen cases were excluded according to predetermined exclusion criteria, resulting in 1206 studies being included in the final analysis (700 males, 520 females). All examinations were performed using a 128-slice CT scanner (Siemens SOMATOM; syngo CT VC 40). CTA protocols included 5-mm acquisition and 1-mm reconstruction, with administration of 100-120 mL of iodinated contrast at 5-6 mL/s via an 18G antecubital cannula. Post-processing involved multiplanar reformation, volume rendering, and 3D reconstruction. Two experienced radiologists independently reviewed all studies. Renal arteries were categorized into Types A-E and Patterns I-V. "Early division" (Types B and E) and "polar branches" (Types C and D) were further grouped for analytical purposes.ResultsAmong 1206 CTA studies, Type A (normal hilar artery) was the most common in both kidneys, with a slightly higher prevalence on the right (74.29%) than on the left (67.99%). Polar branches were more frequent in the left kidney, whereas early divisions were more common in the right kidney. Pattern 1 was predominant bilaterally (RK: 85.73%; LK: 77.61%), followed by Pattern 2. Significant differences were observed between the kidneys in the distribution of Types A, C, D, and Patterns 1 and 2.ConclusionCTA provides excellent visualization of renal artery variations, enabling precise classification and improving surgical, interventional, and transplant planning. Recognition of these anatomical differences is essential for minimizing procedural complications.

items.title: NON-INVASIVE HemodynamicS of Non-Thrombotic Iliac Vein Lesions ARE DISTURBED IN PATIEnTS with A HiSTORY OF Deep Venous Thrombosis.

sections.objective: Non thrombotic iliac vein lesions (NIVL) are thought to be associated with deep vein thrombosis (DVT), yet most individuals with NIVL never develop thrombotic complications. This study assessed whether ultrasound-derived hemodynamic measurements differ between NIVL patients with and without a history of DVT, and whether these hemodynamic measurements better discriminate DVT history than percent stenosis alone.
sections.methods: We performed a retrospective case-control study of patients evaluated at a tertiary academic referral center between 2022 and 2025 who underwent pelvic venous duplex ultrasound imaging. Patients with left common iliac vein stenoses greater than 20 percent were included and categorized by history of left lower extremity DVT. Exclusion criteria included concurrent DVT or prior venous stenting. Ultrasound images were digitized to obtain vessel diameters and spectral Doppler velocities in the iliac veins. Mean velocity, peak velocity, flow rate, shear rate, and ipsilateral and contralateral ratios were calculated. Continuous variables were compared using Welch t tests, with statistical significance defined as p<0.05.
sections.results: 45 patients were included, comprising 9 with prior DVT and 36 without. Amongst all metrics, velocity-based metrics at the compressed left common iliac vein showed the strongest associations with a history of prior DVT, including ipsilateral velocity ratio (log2 fold change -1.539, p=0.007), peak velocity (log2 fold change -0.999, p=0.002), and mean velocity (log2 fold change -0.989, p=0.002). Differences in percent stenosis were statistically significant but less discriminative than velocity-based metrics (log2 fold change 0.363, p=0.033). Composite metrics such as flow rate and shear rate demonstrated weaker discrimination. Dimensionality reduction analysis revealed distinct clustering based on multivariate hemodynamic features between patients with and without a history of DVT.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with NIVL, decreased velocity through the left common iliac vein at the compression point was the strongest predictor of prior DVT whereas percent stenosis was less discriminative. This study suggests that ultrasound-derived hemodynamic assessment can potentially provide a functional framework for risk stratification in patients with NIVL, but further prospective studies are needed to validate its clinical utility.

items.title: A pilot study of the InVera Infusion Device: Twelve-month outcomes in the treatment of incompetent saphenous veins.

sections.objective: The InVera Infusion Device is a novel catheter designed for the delivery of sclerosant agents during non-thermal, non-tumescent (NTNT) ablation of incompetent superficial truncal veins of the lower extremity. This device pilot study aimed to evaluate the technical success, safety, and 12-month clinical outcome.
sections.methods: A single-center, prospective pilot study enrolled 10 patients with primary symptomatic axial reflux who underwent chemical ablation procedures with sclerosant delivery using the InVera Infusion Device. Primary outcomes assessed were technical procedural success, adverse events, Revised Venous Clinical Severity Score (rVCSS), patient-reported outcomes (PROs) based on a HASTI (Heaviness, Achiness, Swelling, Throbbing, Itching) symptom questionnaire and anatomical success rates from duplex ultrasound examination at baseline, 1 week, 8 weeks, 3, 6, and 12 months post procedure. Baseline and 12 months post procedure were compared for both the rVCSS and the HASTI results using a paired t-test and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test respectively RESULTS: Technical procedural success was 100%. There were no device-related adverse events or serious adverse events including no deep vein thrombosis recorded throughout the follow-up period. Clinician assessed rVCSS and patient reported HASTI scores both showed statistically significant reductions from baseline to 12 months (adjusted p = 0.03 for both). Ultrasound-based anatomical assessment at 12 months demonstrated elimination of abnormal reflux and complete or partial occlusion in 90% of patients.
sections.conclusion: The InVera Infusion device provides a safe and effective technique for the delivery of sclerosant agents as part of the management of incompetent saphenous veins, demonstrating favorable 12-month anatomical, clinical and patient reported outcomes in this pilot cohort.

items.title: Systematic Review of Devices, Designs, and Trials for the Treatment of Deep Venous Reflux.

sections.objective: Chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) is driven primarily by venous reflux and affects nearly one-third of adults. While superficial reflux is effectively treated with ablation, therapeutic options for deep venous reflux (DVR) remain limited. Despite decades of innovation, no prosthetic or bioprosthetic venous valve has achieved U.S. regulatory approval. We systematically reviewed device strategies, clinical and hemodynamic outcomes, complications, and barriers to translation for devices designed to treat DVR.
sections.methods: We conducted a PROSPERO-registered systematic review (CRD420251101761) of six databases from inception through February 2026, including in vivo animal and human studies evaluating prosthetic or bioprosthetic devices for DVR. Studies of native valve repair or autotransplantation were excluded. The primary outcome for human studies was clinical improvement, and secondary outcomes included patency, procedural complications, valvular function, and thrombosis.
sections.results: Of 516 records identified, 15 met inclusion criteria: 8 human and 7 animal studies. Two principal strategies were identified: intraluminal valve restoration (VR) and external compression (EC), with approximately 40% of devices delivered percutaneously or endovenously. In human studies, technical success ranged from 87.7%-100%, patency from 67%-100%, and perioperative complication rates from 0%-44%, consisting primarily of bleeding, wound infection, and valve thrombosis. Valve occlusion occurred in up to 28% of animal implants and 18%-22% of select human cohorts. Two perioperative deaths occurred in animal studies; none were reported in human studies. Among human studies, valve competency assessment methods varied substantially. Reported competency ranged from 0%-92%, reflecting heterogeneity in imaging modalities and definitions. Discordance between anatomic patency, duplex-derived reflux reduction, and clinical improvement was frequently observed. In contemporary multicenter trial data, fewer than half of patients met predefined reflux-reduction endpoints despite high device patency and substantial clinical improvement, highlighting discordance between anatomic, hemodynamic, and patient-centered outcomes. By one year, pain had improved in 75%-97% of patients; rVCSS decreased by 37%-81%, with clinically meaningful (≥3-point) improvement in up to 84.6%; and ulcer healing ranged from 67%-100%. Longer follow-up extended to 2 years in animal studies and up to 11 years in human series with various outcomes reported.
sections.conclusion: Several devices developed for DVR have demonstrated technical feasibility and symptom improvement. However, the risk of thrombosis, the marginal impact on valvular function, and the lack of standardization and selection of adequate endpoints in the measurement of results remain major barriers to regulatory approval. Standardized composite endpoints integrating objective hemodynamic measures with patient-centered outcomes are essential to advance durable DVR device development and clinical translation.

items.title: Fertility, pregnancy, and women's health in bronchiectasis: a multicenter study and ELF-EMBARC patient survey.

sections.objective: Bronchiectasis in women of reproductive age is increasingly recognized, yet data on fertility and pregnancy outcomes remain limited.
sections.methods: We conducted a multicenter, retrospective cohort study across EMBARC-affiliated centers including women with bronchiectasis and pregnancy between 2012 and 2023. Clinical, pulmonary, obstetric, and neonatal data were collected. In parallel, an international patient survey assessed fertility, pregnancy, and hormonal influences on disease. Statistical analyses included comparative and correlation testing.
sections.results: Eighty-three women contributed data from 121 pregnancies and 123 neonates. Mean age at conception was 29.5 years. Assisted reproductive technologies were used in 32.1% of pregnancies, more frequently in primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) than other etiologies (48.5% vs. 8.7%, P=0.004). Lung function remained stable during and after pregnancy. Exacerbations occurred in 58.6% of pregnancies. Mean gestational age was 38 weeks and mean birth weight was 2.99 kg. Pre-pregnancy FEV1 correlated with birth weight (ρ=0.42, P=0.001) and gestational age (ρ=0.25, P=0.042). Neonatal outcomes were generally favorable. Survey data (n=629) demonstrated an early onset of menopause in women with bronchiectasis diagnosed before age 50 years compared to after 50 years. Women with PCD reported difficulties conceiving more often than women with early onset bronchiectasis without PCD.
sections.conclusion: Pregnancy in women with bronchiectasis is frequently complicated by exacerbations and low neonatal birth weight. Subfertility is primarily driven by PCD, while non-PCD bronchiectasis shows rates similar to the general population. Pre-pregnancy lung function is associated with neonatal outcomes, supporting the importance of pulmonary optimization and multidisciplinary care before and during pregnancy.
sections.other: What are fertility characteristics, pregnancy outcomes, and patient-reported reproductive health experiences in women with bronchiectasis?

items.title: Striving for Equity in Cystic Fibrosis Research: Perspectives from Black and Hispanic/ Latino(a) Individuals with CF.

sections.objective: Black and Hispanic people with cystic fibrosis (PwCF) experience worse health outcomes. Health disparities are exacerbated by clinical research that does not adequately represent the diversity of the CF population.
sections.methods: Semi-structured, individual interviews were conducted with PwCF aged ≥18 years who identify as Black/African American race and/or Hispanic/Latino(a) ethnicity. Participants were recruited from six geographically diverse CF centers and through CF Foundation Community Voice, a CF community partner organization. The interview guide was created by a committee that included minoritized PwCF, research coordinators, and physician-scientists. Thematic analysis with inductive and deductive coding was used to analyze interview transcripts.
sections.results: Twenty PwCF were interviewed from 2024 to 2025. Drawing from a race-conscious adaptation of the Behavioral Model for Vulnerable Populations, we used domains of predisposing, need-based, and healthcare environment factors, as well as emergent themes relating to information and support needs. Participants discussed barriers to research participation that included narrow eligibility criteria (e.g., genotype requirements, health status) and logistical challenges such as time and cost. PwCF described a sense of isolation as persons of color with CF, which impacted sense of trust in CF care and research studies. They highlighted that racialized experiences, especially doubt surrounding their CF diagnosis, significantly impact willingness to participate. Solutions center around providing community support to address feelings of isolation and information needs to provide transparency about study design and intent.
sections.conclusion: Participation in clinical research is strongly influenced by an interplay of social, cultural, health, and systemic factors. Solutions to improve inclusion in trials center the needs of marginalized communities across all phases of study design and implementation.
sections.other: How do Black/African American and Hispanic/Latino(a) PwCF perceive clinical research? What are the barriers and facilitators to participation in research? Are there viable solutions to improve inclusion?

items.title: Risk Factors for Retinal Pigment Epithelium Tears in Patients with Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

sections.methods: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines and was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251075278). MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to December 15, 2025. Randomized and non-randomized studies of adults (≥50 years) with nAMD evaluating candidate predictors of RPE tear were included. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (RoB 2, ROBINS-I). Random-effects meta-analyses were performed for baseline PED height and area, with per-study weighting, standardized mean difference (SMD), and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses. Certainty was assessed using GRADE.
sections.results: Sixteen studies comprising 4,043 eyes were included. Five studies (55 tear eyes; 370 controls; 425 eyes) showed greater baseline PED height in eyes developing tears (mean difference [MD], 212.39 µm; 95% confidence interval [CI], 133.87-290.91; I² = 24.6%; SMD, 1.09). Four studies (48 tear eyes; 1,312 controls; 1,360 eyes) showed larger baseline PED area (MD, 5.80 mm²; 95% CI, 3.48-8.12; I² = 2.7%; SMD, 0.88). Both persisted across all leave-one-out iterations; omitting the study contributing 43.5% of the area weight increased the effect (MD, 7.11 mm²). Fibrovascular PED, greater basal diameter and volume, subretinal fluid, sub-RPE clefts, radial hyperreflective lines, and occult or hemorrhagic macular neovascularization were also associated with tears. Anti-VEGF agent selection was not consistently associated. Most studies were at moderate to serious risk of bias; certainty was very low.
sections.conclusion: Baseline PED morphology, particularly increased height, is the most consistently reported association with RPE tear in nAMD. Because the evidence is predominantly retrospective, largely unadjusted, and of very low certainty, these are associations rather than validated predictive markers. Prospective studies using standardized imaging protocols are needed.
sections.other: To identify and synthesize clinical, imaging, and treatment-related risk factors associated with retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) tears in neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD). RPE tears are a vision-threatening complication of nAMD, occurring most often in eyes with pigment epithelial detachments (PEDs) and frequently temporally associated with initiation of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy. Improved recognition of high-risk PED features may enhance counseling and risk stratification.

items.title: Nail disorders in pediatric patients: Part 1. Clinical overview, diagnosis and management of physiological variants, and congenital, hereditary, and infectious etiologies.
items.abstract: Nail disorders in children are relatively common and anxiety-provoking for families, yet frequently underrecognized in clinical practice. Many nail disorders in children require no treatment or are readably treatable; however, unfamiliarity may lead to unnecessary, inappropriate, or delayed treatment. In this part 1 of a 2-part continuing medical education series we review physiological variants and congenital, hereditary, and infectious nail disorders, and provide diagnostic and management tips for dermatologists managing these conditions.
keywords: congenital hypertrophy of the nail folds
congenital malalignment of the great toenail

items.title: Psoriasis: Which therapy for which patient, updated, part I. Focus on Psoriasis Comorbidities and Preferred Systemic Agents.
items.abstract: Patients with psoriasis (PsO) may have various comorbidities, that are either related to or unrelated to the disease itself. Selection of the appropriate treatment modality has evolved substantially with the rapid expansion of available options that can be individualized based on patients' comorbidity profiles, extent of disease, prior therapeutic response, and treatment preferences. This first article of a two-part series focuses on selecting systemic therapy for PsO patients with specific inflammatory comorbidities or a history of malignancy.

items.title: Nail disorders in pediatric patients: Part 2. Clinical overview, diagnosis and management of inflammatory, pigmentary, and neoplastic etiologies.
items.abstract: Nail disorders represent a relatively uncommon but diverse group of conditions seen in pediatric patients. Management varies largely by etiology. Some inflammatory nail disorders in children are self-limited, whereas others may lead to permanent nail loss if not recognized and treated early. In addition, certain nail disorders may present differently in children than adults and may suggest increased systemic disease burden. In Part 2 of this two-part continuing medical education series, we review inflammatory, pigmentary, and neoplastic nail disorders in children and propose clinical approach algorithms for pediatric nail psoriasis and longitudinal melanonychia.

items.title: Distinct patterns of whole-body coding in human motor cortex and posterior parietal cortex.
items.abstract: Traditional views of cortical motor areas hold that movements of different parts of the body, or effectors, are represented in distinct anatomical locations. The extent of overlap in effector representations has been a topic of debate for decades. We recorded from single neurons in hand areas of the motor cortex (MC) and posterior parietal cortex (PPC) of tetraplegic humans while they attempted movements across the body. We found a population response to every movement tested in both areas; however, the hand knob of MC more selectively responded to hand movements, whereas PPC represented all effectors strongly. Single neurons in MC responded selectively to a single effector or to two effectors that were part of the same limb. In PPC, neurons exhibited mixed selectivity, responding to combinations of effectors. These findings suggest a transition from a highly effector-general representation in PPC to regional effector specificity in MC.

items.title: An acetylcholine-inhibited sleep-active hippocampal interneuron orchestrates memory consolidation.
items.abstract: Memory reactivation during hippocampal ripples is critical for sleep-dependent memory consolidation. However, the molecular-to-circuit mechanism enabling sleep-predominant ripple generation remains unresolved. Here, we discovered that a sparse population of GABAergic interneurons in the mouse hippocampus specializes in gating ripple generation and memory consolidation. While all known genetically labeled hippocampal interneurons were highly active during wakefulness and rapid-eye-movement (REM) sleep, genetic targeting of M2 acetylcholine receptor (Chrm2)-expressing neurons isolated a specific population preferentially active during non-REM (NREM) sleep and quiet wakefulness. These acetylcholine-inhibited interneurons inhibited the entire hippocampus in an infra-slow rhythm (∼0.015 Hz). Suppressing their activity in dorsal CA3 or ventral hippocampus impaired spatial and social memory, respectively. Furthermore, Chrm2+ neurons were closely associated with ripples; their activity bidirectionally modulated ripple occurrence via widespread inhibition. Thus, Chrm2+ interneurons are critical in linking neuromodulatory state to memory consolidation, offering genetically targeted access to sleep-active memory circuits implicated in cognitive disorders.

items.title: The perceived impact of extreme weather events on care for people with HIV or tuberculosis and HIV in Zimbabwe: a survey-based multicentre cross-sectional observational study and formative evaluation.

sections.objective: The growing threat to health systems posed by extreme weather events (EWEs) disproportionately affects people living with HIV and tuberculosis disease in high-burden, low-resource settings. In Zimbabwe, for example, the 2023-24 El Niño-induced drought intensified food insecurity and reduced access to clinics and medication for such vulnerable populations. We aimed to conduct a formative evaluation to assess the perceived impact of climate change and EWEs on HIV and tuberculosis determinants and service delivery and identify potential climate-adaptive health-service strategies.
sections.methods: In this survey-based multicentre cross-sectional observational study with a formative evaluation supplemented by qualitative data, we surveyed people living with HIV from Sept 19 to Dec 19, 2024, across 321 clinics in Zimbabwe to describe their perceived impact of EWEs on their health. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling. The inclusion criteria were being diagnosed with HIV, being older than 18 years, and receiving HIV care at Organization for Public Health Interventions and Development (OPHID) clinics during the study period. Individuals who were not receiving HIV care at an OPHID clinic or who were younger than 18 years were excluded. A client satisfaction survey was used to collect data from in-person surveys. The survey included questions related to the general effects of EWEs, such as drought, extreme heat, and flooding; how EWEs had affected HIV or tuberculosis care; and what, if any, services were currently available or should be made available to mitigate climate impacts on health. We also conducted six focus group discussions (FGDs; five to eight participants per group) between March 12 and May 12, 2024, across the Bulilima, Mangwe, and Matobo districts. We used a convenience sampling approach to select patients who had visited the health facility for medical check-ups, medication resupply, or viral load testing, as recorded in clinical registers and verified by clinical staff. Eligible participants for the FGDs were adults (≥18 years) with HIV, or with current or previous tuberculosis treatment, receiving care at the study facility during the recruitment period; those under 18 years or not receiving care at the facility were excluded. Participants' sex was self-reported at enrolment. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively, whereas FGD data were analysed using a modified framework approach. The main outcomes were the perceived impact of climate change and EWEs on HIV and tuberculosis determinants and service delivery outcomes, as reported by affected communities, and community-prioritised mitigation strategies to feasibly address climate-sensitive determinants and barriers to care.
sections.results: Among 1804 eligible participants approached across 15 districts, all completed the survey and were included in the analysis. Most survey participants (1363 [75·6%] of 1804 participants) reported noticing changes in climate over the past 5 years; of these 1363 participants, 900 (66·0%) were female and 1024 (75·1%) participants reported disruptions to their HIV care during the time they noticed changes in climate. Survey respondents reported that climate-related disruptions were associated with increased food insecurity (reported by 877 [85·6%] of 1024 participants) and water shortage (667 [65·1%] of 1024 participants). Qualitative analysis confirmed that the barriers to HIV and tuberculosis care from EWEs included widespread food insecurity, crop failures, and livestock deaths, with consequent effects on income leading to challenges in paying for food and transportation to clinics. Participants highlighted the need for expanded services that facilitate social and economic wellbeing, including nutrition support, water access, transportation, and income-generating activities, and decentralised models of health-care delivery.
sections.conclusion: Extreme heat and drought affect food and water security and have financial implications, creating challenges for patients to access care in Zimbabwe. Our findings underscore the urgent need for integrated, climate-adaptive strategies to maintain HIV and tuberculosis care in such climate-vulnerable regions.

items.title: Updated treatment targets in inflammatory bowel disease (STRIDE-III): an initiative of the International Organization for the Study of IBD.
items.abstract: Since Selecting Therapeutic Targets in Inflammatory Bowel Disease-II (STRIDE-II), new evidence has become available across inflammatory and patient-centred outcomes. We aimed to update the STRIDE recommendations for Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL for studies published after the STRIDE-II search period. Findings were integrated with surveys of International Organization for the Study of IBD (IOIBD) members and paediatric gastroenterologists from the Porto group of the European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition. Statements were subsequently voted on using a modified Delphi approach; consensus was defined as ≥75% of participants rating a statement 7-10 on a 10-point scale. Of 13 071 records identified in the systematic review, 1018 were included. Surveys were completed by 60 of 79 IOIBD gastroenterologists and 23 of 30 paediatric gastroenterologists in the Porto group. STRIDE-III defines three conceptually distinct categories of treatment targets. Actionable targets include clinical response and remission, which reflect patient priorities, and objective inflammatory targets (C-reactive protein normalisation, faecal calprotectin within target range, and endoscopic remission), supported by interventional evidence demonstrating benefits of target-guided treatment modification. Adjunctive targets (ie, urgency, histological remission in ulcerative colitis, transmural remission in Crohn's disease, and growth) are supported by studies showing association with favourable outcomes and guide treatment optimisation and tighter monitoring but do not necessarily require a change in therapeutic class. Patient-centred targets (ie, disability, fatigue, and quality of life) directly reflect patients' well-being and are impaired in a substantial proportion of patients with inflammatory bowel disease; impairment should prompt assessment of inflammation and alternative causes and management through shared decision-making. Targets are further classified as immediate, short-term, intermediate, and long-term. STRIDE-III also defines treatment-specific times to target achievement, new faecal calprotectin thresholds, and adaptations for resource-limited settings. STRIDE-III distinguishes targets that should prompt treatment change from those that primarily guide optimisation and monitoring, while establishing a separate patient-centred pathway based on shared decision-making. This framework supports consistent, evidence-based treat-to-target care.

items.title: The development of obesity pharmacotherapy: from early challenges and setbacks to recognition by WHO.
items.abstract: Obesity is a chronic, progressive disease associated with disability, increased morbidity, and reduced life expectancy. Global prevalence has risen sharply in recent decades, yet obesity and its treatment-particularly pharmacotherapy -have been highly stigmatised. A legacy of early medications withdrawn over safety concerns, together with poor efficacy, and widespread lack of recognition of obesity as a chronic disease contributed to persistent underuse of obesity pharmacotherapy. This underuse changed in the 2020s with GLP-1 receptor agonists and, later, multiagonist therapies, with their substantially greater efficacy, safety, and disease-modifying benefits compared with older agents. Reflecting this paradigm shift, WHO issued global guidelines and included GLP-1 receptor agonists in the Essential Medicines List, albeit for a narrowly defined population. We take a critical historical perspective, charting the highs and lows of obesity medication development and examining the scientific, regulatory, and societal factors that have slowed or impeded the translation of pharmacological advances into safe, effective, and widely accepted treatments for obesity.

items.title: Oropouche virus infection in pregnant women in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: a prospective cohort study.

sections.objective: Although adverse maternal and infant outcomes have been reported following Oropouche virus infection, the frequencies of these outcomes have not been compared with those in uninfected pregnancies. We followed up pregnant women from areas with Oropouche virus transmission in Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil, to evaluate potential adverse maternal and infant outcomes following Oropouche virus exposure.
sections.methods: In this prospective cohort study across the state of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, we included pregnant women receiving prenatal care in municipalities with or at high risk of Oropouche virus outbreaks. Inclusion criteria were: ongoing risk of Oropouche virus infection at the time of prenatal visit; prenatal care at one of the participating sites; and willingness and ability to consent to and participate in the study. Exclusion criteria included infection with other arboviruses and fetal chromosomal abnormalities. Maternal blood, urine, and saliva were collected and tested for Oropouche virus by RT-PCR at enrolment and pregnancy endpoints. IgG and IgM serologies from maternal blood, placental tissue PCR, and immunohistochemistry were done. Confirmed infections were defined by: positive Oropouche virus PCR in blood, urine, saliva, or placenta; positive Oropouche virus placental immunohistochemistry; or Oropouche virus-specific IgM or IgG seroconversion. Possible infection was defined as one positive IgM result without a positive PCR. Negative results ruled out infection. Adverse maternal outcomes (reported by study investigators following up participants at study sites) were maternal death or disability, fetal loss, or haemorrhage; adverse infant outcomes were neonatal death or malformations. Relative risks adjusted for maternal age, other congenital infections, and use of tobacco, alcohol, and drugs during pregnancy for adverse maternal and infant outcomes were calculated.
sections.results: Between Nov 29, 2024, and Oct 8, 2025, 544 participants were enrolled: 130 (24%) with confirmed, 143 (26%) with possible, and 271 (50%) with no Oropouche virus infection. The median cycle threshold value of RT-PCR was 29·7 (IQR 25·8-34·9). Among the 130 women with confirmed infection, 104 (80%) developed detectable IgG antibodies. Symptoms were present in 80 (62%) women with confirmed infection, not necessarily associated with adverse outcomes (adjusted relative risk [aRR] 0∙84 [95% credible interval 0∙51-1∙21]). By the end of follow-up, the pregnancies of 119 women with confirmed infection and 193 with no infection had resulted in livebirth, stillbirth, or miscarriage; 105 (88%) women with confirmed infection had livebirths and 187 (97%) women without infection had livebirths. Adverse maternal outcomes occurred in 21 (18%) women with confirmed infection and 14 (7%) women with no infection (aRR 2∙90 [1∙52-5∙35]). Fetal loss and haemorrhage risk were three times higher in women with confirmed infection than in those with no infection (aRR 3∙08 [1∙28-7∙29] for fetal loss and 2∙79 [1∙22-6∙21] for haemorrhage). The aRR for adverse infant outcomes was 9∙18 (1∙89-47∙88). CNS abnormalities occurred in eight (8%) infants of mothers with confirmed infection and in no infants of mothers with no infection.
sections.conclusion: Oropouche virus infection during pregnancy is associated with severe maternal and infant outcomes, including maternal haemorrhage, fetal loss, and infant CNS abnormalities.
sections.other: For the Portuguese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

items.title: 8 weeks versus 12 weeks of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir for treatment-naive, non-cirrhotic, chronic hepatitis C (RESOLVE): a multicentre, open-label, non-inferiority, randomised controlled trial in India.

sections.objective: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection without cirrhosis can be treated with 12 weeks of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir combination therapy. We aimed to assess whether a shorter 8-week treatment regimen of this combination was non-inferior to the standard 12-week regimen in successfully clearing HCV infection in HCV-infected patients without evidence of cirrhosis.
sections.methods: RESOLVE was a multicentre, open-label, non-inferiority, randomised controlled trial, conducted in five publicly funded hospitals in India. We randomly assigned (1:1) treatment-naive adults (aged ≥18 years) with non-cirrhotic HCV mono-infection to receive sofosbuvir 400 mg and velpatasvir 100 mg (orally, daily) for either 8 weeks or 12 weeks. The primary outcome was the proportion of participants with sustained virological response-ie, absence of quantifiable HCV RNA at 12 weeks after treatment completion (SVR12), with 95% assumed proportion with 12-week treatment, 5% non-inferiority margin, 2·5% one-sided alpha error, and 90% study power in the per-protocol population. The trial was registered with the Clinical Trial Registry of India, CTRI/2022/03/041368, and is complete.
sections.results: Between May 15, 2022, and Sept 10, 2024, we screened 1620 participants, of whom 880 (54·3%) were enrolled in the study and randomly assigned to the 12-week (n=437 [50%]) or 8-week (n=443 [50%]) groups. 455 (52%) participants were women, 425 (48%) were men, and the median age was 35 years (IQR 28 to 47). 816 (93%) participants completed the intended 12-week (401 [92%] of 437) or 8-week (415 [94%] of 443) treatment and SVR12 testing. On per-protocol analysis, the proportion reaching SVR12 with 8-week treatment (410/415; 98·8% [95% CI 97·2 to 99·6]) was non-inferior to 12-week treatment (397/401; 99·0% [97·5 to 99·7]), with a risk difference of 0·2% (-1·5 to 1·9). Further, on intention-to-treat analysis, the proportion of participants reaching SVR12 with 8-week treatment (414/443; 93·5% [90·9 to 95·5]) was non-inferior to 12-week treatment (401/437; 91·8% [88·8 to 94·2]) with a risk difference of -1·7% (-5·2 to 1·9). No participant had any drug-related serious adverse event or drug discontinuation due to an adverse event.
sections.conclusion: An 8-week regimen of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir was similar in efficacy to the standard 12-week treatment in individuals with chronic HCV infection without cirrhosis. This finding supports shortening the duration of treatment in such patients.

items.title: Cardiovascular safety of orforglipron versus insulin glargine in adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk (ACHIEVE-4): a phase 3, event-driven, randomised, open-label, non-inferiority, active comparator trial.

sections.objective: Orforglipron is an oral, non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist. While some peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists have established cardiovascular benefit, the cardiovascular safety of non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists has not been studied. This study aimed to compare the effect of orforglipron with insulin glargine on the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events in individuals with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight who are at increased risk for cardiovascular events.
sections.methods: This event-driven, phase 3, multicentre, randomised, open-label, active comparator, parallel-group study was conducted in 317 sites across 16 countries and territories. Adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk with glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) concentrations between 7·0% and 10·5% (53-91 mmol/mol) and a BMI of 25 kg/m2 or more, treated with up to three glucose-lowering medications (metformin, a sulfonylurea, and/or an SGLT2 inhibitor), were randomly assigned (1:1) to oral orforglipron maximum tolerated dose (up to 36 mg capsule [equivalent to 17·2 mg tablet]) or injectable titrated insulin glargine, each administered once daily. All participants had established cardiovascular or chronic kidney disease. The primary outcome was time to occurrence of four-component major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE-4), including cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for unstable angina. Non-inferiority of orforglipron to insulin glargine was declared if the upper limit of the two-sided 95% CI for the hazard ratio (HR; orforglipron vs insulin glargine) was less than 1·8. The primary endpoint and other safety endpoints were assessed in all participants who took at least one dose of assigned treatment using all datapoints from baseline until withdrawal or study completion, regardless of treatment adherence. This trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05803421) and is completed.
sections.results: Between May 1, 2023, and Sept 5, 2024, 2749 participants were randomly assigned (1371 to orforglipron and 1378 to insulin glargine). 1032 (38%) participants were female and 1717 (62·5%) male. 2362 (85·9%) participants had established cardiovascular disease and 1033 (37·6%) had chronic kidney disease. Mean baseline age, HbA1c, and BMI were 63·1 years (SD 9·9), 8·2% (1·0), and 33 kg/m2 (6·2), respectively. Over a median follow-up of 2 years, the primary outcome occurred in 57 (4·2%) of 1358 orforglipron participants and 67 (5·0%) of 1343 insulin glargine participants, showing non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4 (HR 0·84; 95% CI 0·59-1·20; p<0·0001 for non-inferiority). Gastrointestinal adverse events were reported in 851 (62·1%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 193 (14·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants; clinically significant or severe hypoglycaemia (glucose <3 mmol/L [54 mg/dL]) occurred in 93 (6·8%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 260 (19·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants. 62 deaths were reported during the study: 19 (1·4%) of 1371 participants receiving orforglipron and 43 (3·2%) of 1355 participants receiving insulin glargine; all deaths except one (in the insulin glargine group) were deemed unrelated to treatment.
sections.conclusion: In people with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk, the cardiovascular safety of orforglipron was confirmed by demonstrating non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most frequent adverse event and most common reason for orforglipron treatment discontinuation with orforglipron, while clinically significant hypoglycaemia occurred less frequently with orforglipron than with insulin glargine. These findings support orforglipron as a potential once-daily, oral treatment option with established cardiovascular safety in people with type 2 diabetes and increased cardiovascular risk.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of garetosmab, an activin A-blocking antibody, in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (OPTIMA): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) is an ultrarare genetic disorder resulting in progressive heterotopic ossification of ligaments, tendons, and muscles, leading to disability and early mortality. FOP is caused by heterozygous gain-of-function mutations in the activin receptor type 1A, allowing this receptor to be aberrantly activated by activin A (ActA), which normally inhibits this receptor, thus driving heterotopic bone formation. In preclinical models and an earlier phase 2 trial (LUMINA-1) in FOP, an antibody blocking ActA (garetosmab) prevented heterotopic ossification. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of garetosmab in adults living with FOP.
sections.methods: OPTIMA is a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial conducted at 18 study sites across 16 countries and regions. Participants aged 18 years or older with FOP were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to monthly intravenous placebo, garetosmab 3 mg/kg, or garetosmab 10 mg/kg. Randomisation was stratified by baseline Cumulative Analogue Joint Involvement Scale score and previous participation in the LUMINA-1 study. The primary efficacy and safety endpoints were total number of new heterotopic bone lesions at week 56 and treatment-emergent adverse events of special interest (AESIs) through week 56, analysed in all randomised participants who received at least one dose of the study drug. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05394116); the trial is active (completed primary endpoint) but not recruiting participants.
sections.results: Between Nov 21, 2022, and July 4, 2024, 63 participants were enrolled and randomly assigned (placebo, n=21; garetosmab 3 mg/kg, n=19; garetosmab 10 mg/kg, n=23). The mean age was 26·6 years (SD 6·8); 38 (60%) participants were female and 25 (40%) male. 62 participants completed 56 weeks of treatment; one participant in the placebo group discontinued at 53 weeks. The total number of new heterotopic bone lesions was significantly lower with garetosmab: there were 19 lesions with placebo versus one lesion with garetosmab 3 mg/kg (rate ratio vs placebo: 0·06 [95% CI 0·00-0·73]; p=0·027) and two lesions with garetosmab 10 mg/kg (rate ratio vs placebo: 0·10 [0·01-0·76]; p=0·026). Treatment-emergent AESIs occurred in one (5%) of 21 participants receiving placebo, zero of 19 receiving garetosmab 3 mg/kg, and four (17%) of 23 receiving garetosmab 10 mg/kg; all were considered treatment-related. No deaths occurred.
sections.conclusion: Garetosmab substantially reduced the number of new heterotopic bone lesions, providing robust evidence of its potential to be an efficacious and generally well tolerated disease-modifying therapy for FOP.

items.title: Immunogenicity of fractional one-fifth and one-half doses of 17DD yellow fever vaccine compared with full dose in children aged 9-23 months in Uganda: a phase 4, single-blind, randomised clinical trial.

sections.objective: Fractional doses of yellow fever vaccines have been shown to be safe and immunogenic in randomised controlled trials in adults and children. However, little evidence still remains in children younger than 2 years. We assessed immunogenicity of one-fifth (0·1 mL) and one-half (0·25 mL) fractional doses compared with full doses of 17DD yellow fever vaccine in children aged 9-23 months in Kampala, Uganda.
sections.methods: This phase 4, single-blind, randomised clinical trial evaluating fractional dose 17DD yellow fever vaccine among children was conducted at three public-sector health facilities in Uganda. Eligible participants were aged 9-23 months at enrolment, had no history of yellow fever disease or vaccination, and did not meet the exclusion criteria. Children were enrolled in three age strata: 9-12 months, 13-18 months, and 19-23 months, and were randomly assigned (1:1:1) using block randomisation (block sizes of three and six) to one-fifth (0·1 mL), one-half (0·25 mL), or full (0·5 mL) doses of the 17DD yellow fever vaccine. Participants were followed up at 4 weeks (visit 1 [V1]), 1 year (visit 2 [V2]), and 13-48 months (visit 3 [V3]) after vaccination. The primary analysis included per-protocol participants who attended within the prespecified visit window; an intention-to-treat analysis was also conducted including all randomly assigned participants with available outcome data. Participants with missing serological data were excluded from the analysis at the corresponding visit. The primary outcome was non-inferiority in seroconversion (5 percentage-point margin) at V1 measured by 50% plaque reduction neutralisation test. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03725618, and is complete.
sections.results: Between March 26, 2019, and May 11, 2021, 1784 participants were randomly assigned to either one-fifth dose (n=600), one-half dose (n=594), or full dose (n=590). The median (IQR) age at enrolment was 13 (11-18) months. Both fractional doses met the non-inferiority criterion compared with the full dose with no difference in seroconversion between one-fifth and full doses and -0·17 (95% CI -0·52 to 0·17) difference between one-half and full doses in the per-protocol population at V1. There was no difference between the one-fifth and full doses.
sections.conclusion: Both fractional doses of 17DD yellow fever vaccine were non-inferior to full doses in inducing initial seroconversion. The results support the use of fractional dose yellow fever vaccines among young children for outbreak response during supply shortages.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of litifilimab in cutaneous lupus erythematosus: 24-week results of the randomized phase 2 study, AMETHYST.

sections.objective: Cutaneous lupus erythematosus (CLE) is a serious autoimmune disease with no approved targeted treatments. Evaluate the efficacy and safety of litifilimab in AMETHYST Part A (Phase 2).
sections.methods: AMETHYST is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, Phase 2/3 study that investigates litifilimab in participants with CLE. Participants were randomized to receive litifilimab 225 mg or placebo every 4 weeks during Weeks 0-24. The primary endpoint was the Cutaneous Lupus Activity Investigator's Global Assessment-Revised (CLA-IGA-R) erythema score of 0-1 at Week 16, with several Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus Disease Area and Severity Index (CLASI)-based endpoints at Week 24 as secondary endpoints. Safety was also assessed.
sections.results: Significantly more participants treated with litifilimab achieved clear/almost clear skin (CLA-IGA-R erythema 0-1) than those treated with placebo at Week 16 (14.7% vs 2.9%, P= .0263). Additionally, more participants treated with litifilimab achieved CLASI-70 response vs placebo at Week 24 (21.7% vs 5.8%, P = .0195). Litifilimab was generally well tolerated; safety data were consistent with prior studies.
sections.conclusion: Litifilimab treatment led to greater improvements in skin disease activity vs placebo and was well tolerated in participants with CLE through Week 24.
sections.other: Study was not powered to detect statistically significant differences in secondary endpoints.

items.title: Effect of clarithromycin on the circulating inflammatory proteome in community-acquired pneumonia: a secondary analysis of the ACCESS trial.

sections.objective: The ACCESS randomized double-blind controlled trial in hospitalized adults with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) showed that adding clarithromycin to standard-of-care therapy accelerated clinical recovery within the first 72 hours after the commencement of treatment and reduced progression to organ dysfunction.
sections.methods: Serum samples obtained from ACCESS trial patients at baseline and 72 hours were profiled using the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel. Patients were grouped by treatment arm and by achievement of the trial's composite primary endpoint. After quality control, 70 proteins from 394 paired samples across 197 patients were analyzed to assess differential expression within and between groups over time, evaluate associations with clinical outcomes, and identify immune endotypes using unsupervised clustering.
sections.results: IL6 was selectively downregulated on day 4 in the clarithromycin arm, whereas IFN-γ, CXCL9, CXCL10, and SCF decreased over time across both treatment arms, consistent with resolution of inflammation. Among patients achieving the primary endpoint, IL6, CXCL9, CXCL10, and IFN-γ were suppressed only in clarithromycin-treated individuals. Clustering consistently identified two inflammatory endotypes with comparable SOFA, but distinct RSS scores. The endotype with lower RSS demonstrated higher IFN-γ and globally elevated inflammatory protein expression; in that endotype 90-day mortality was decreased with clarithromycin treatment.
sections.conclusion: Clarithromycin exerts measurable immunomodulatory effects in CAP, characterized by attenuation of pro-inflammatory cytokines, particularly IL6. The identification of distinct inflammatory endotypes suggests biological heterogeneity in CAP and supports future investigation of endotype-guided approaches to identify patients most likely to benefit from immunomodulatory therapies.
sections.other: Does clarithromycin treatment modulate the circulating inflammatory protein profile in CAP, and can inflammatory endotypes identify patient subgroups with distinct clinical responses?

items.title: Retrieval of Thrombosed Inferior Vena Cava Filter and Mechanical Thrombectomy of Associated Caval Thrombosis Using FlowTriever and ClotTriever Systems With the ClotTriever as Embolic Protection.
items.abstract: A 55-year-old Chinese male with anti-phospholipid syndrome presented with left lower limb deep venous thrombosis (DVT) on warfarin and had an inferior vena cava filter (IVCF) implanted before a radical resection of a perineal sarcoma. The inferior vena cava (IVC) filter removal was attempted 2 weeks after the surgery, but thrombus was found at the filter. It was decided to leave the filter and to continue with anticoagulation. He presented with progressive right lower limb swelling, erythema and pain, with a CT venogram showing caval thrombosis extending from the IVC filter to the right below-knee veins. In view of worsening symptoms, endovenous mechanical thrombectomy of the IVC and iliofemoral veins, as well as caval filter removal, was performed using the ClotTriever and FlowTriever devices (Inari Medical, US). The ClotTriever itself was then placed alongside a 16Fr internal jugular vein (IJV) sheath to remove the thrombosed filter. The FlowTriever disc was next deployed from jugular access as proximal embolic protection during the thrombectomy procedure. The procedure was successful with no symptoms of pulmonary embolism (PE). This report illustrates the alternative use of the ClotTriever BOLD as an intra-operative proximal embolic protection in the absence of alternative devices like a ProTrieve sheath, during caval thrombectomy and removal for caval thrombosis secondary to an IVC filter.Clinical ImpactThe ClotTriever BOLD catheter, deployed alongside a large retrograde sheath may be considered as an proximal embolic protection for removing thrombosed IVCFs, where there is patient with a suitably sized IVC and when alternative and appropriate devices are unavailable.

items.title: Comparison of mid-term outcomes of different patch types for endarterectomy of the common femoral artery. Secondary analysis from the ARISTON multicentre registry.

sections.objective: We sought to analyze patients who underwent femoral endarterectomy (FEA) for common femoral artery disease (CFAD) within the multicentre ARISTON registry aiming to compare the short-term and mid-term outcomes based on the use of different patch materials.
sections.methods: The study is a secondary analysis of patients from a retrospective multicentre observational registry of FEA with patch angioplasty, extracted the ARISTON collaborative. The primary endpoint of the study was clinically-driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR).
sections.results: A total of 547 patients undergoing FEA with patch angioplasty were included in the analysis and stratified according to the patch material into three groups: (i) prosthetic patch or PP (group A, n=249), (ii) bovine pericardium patch or BPP (group B, n=262), and (iii) great saphenous vein patch or GSVP (group C, n=36). Baseline characteristics differed significantly among groups. Technical success of the FEA procedure was achieved in all cases. Perioperative mortality was low and not significantly different between groups. Kaplan-Meier estimates of freedom from CD-TLR at two years were 86.2% (95% CI, 80.8-90.2%) in the PP group, 88.9% (95% CI, 83.1-92.8%) in the BPP group, and 69.8% (95% CI, 49.3-83.3%) in the GSVP group, with no statistically significant difference between groups (log-rank p=0.067). In multivariable analysis for freedom from CD-TLR, neither BPP (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.47-1.29; P=0.330) nor GSVP (HR 1.99, 95% CI 0.95-4.17; P=0.069) was significantly associated with the outcome.
sections.conclusion: In this contemporary multicentre real-world experience, PP and BPP were the most used materials for patch reconstruction after FEA in patients with primary CFAD. Although the distribution of baseline risk factors was different between groups, mid-term freedom from CD-TLR was not significantly different between-groups. The findings describe contemporary surgeon-selected practice but do not determine the optimal allocation strategy, thereby reinforcing a clinically relevant message for contemporary vascular surgery: appropriate patient selection, meticulous technical execution, and comprehensive revascularization strategy are the key drivers of clinical outcomes, whereas patch material should likely be regarded as a complementary component within an individualized reconstructive framework.

items.title: Asymptomatic vs. Symptomatic Carotid Revascularization: A Single Institution Retrospective Review.

sections.objective: While carotid revascularization reduces stroke risk in both asymptomatic (AD) and symptomatic (SD) carotid disease, its role continues to evolve with advances in medical therapy, surgical techniques, and cost considerations.
sections.methods: This retrospective study reviews outcomes of patients undergoing revascularization at a level one stroke center between 2019 and 2024. Primary endpoints were ipsilateral stroke, myocardial infarction, and death at 30-day, 90-day, and 1-year. Secondary endpoints include restenosis rates.
sections.results: 113 patients underwent 127 carotid endarterectomies. Sixty-four percent presented with SD, with a median time to intervention of 9 days (IQR 6-11). SD patients had a longer median length of stay (2 vs 1 day, p = 0.076. Follow-up rates were higher in AD at 1 year (65% vs 36%, p = 0.003). MI rates were 0% at 30- and 90-day and 0.9% at 1-year. Stroke rates were 0.9%, 0.9%, and 1.8% at 30-day, 90-day, and one year, with no difference between AD vs SD. 1-year mortality rates were 0.9% and 5.3% at 90-day and one year, without a difference by AD vs SD. Restenosis occurred in 4% of patients, with no difference between groups.
sections.conclusion: Carotid endarterectomy was associated with low perioperative rates of ipsilateral stroke, MI, and death. Despite a longer LOS, SD patients did not have significantly different outcomes or restenosis rates. While males had improved follow-up rates, there was no significant difference in outcomes by gender or race. These findings support favorable outcomes following CEA in both AD and SD.

items.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) and the choroidal challenge: A comprehensive review of AI applications in choroidal imaging.
items.abstract: The choroid is a densely vascular layer that sustains the outer retina and may reflect systemic microvascular health. With the advent of new imaging techniques, choroidal imaging has become increasingly detailed, generating vast data volumes. Conventional analytic tools often fall short in managing these high-dimensional datasets. Artificial intelligence (AI) automatically enhances, segments, and analyzes choroidal images, facilitating the discovery of choroidal biomarkers relevant to ocular and systemic disease. Yet, anatomical complexity, heterogeneous protocols, and a lack of large, annotated datasets hinder AI adoption. Overcoming these barriers is essential to assess AI-derived choroidal biomarkers as reliable diagnostic and prognostic tools.

items.title: Midterm Outcomes of the Minos Ultralow Profile Endograft: Results from the Multicentre MINER Registry.

sections.objective: The aim of this study was to assess midterm outcomes of the ultralow profile Minos endograft in a physician initiated registry.
sections.methods: A non-sponsored registry collected consecutive patients treated with the Minos device in 20 Italian centres (2021 - 2025). Elective patients (the primary analysis population) were stratified by access quality (hostile vs. standard access); hostile iliac-femoral access was defined by a narrowest iliac diameter 1.6, aortic bifurcation diameter < 16 mm, or severe circumferential calcification. Proximal neck features were covariates only; urgent and emergent procedures were analysed separately. Outcomes were thirty day technical success, mortality, and major adverse events (MAEs), and midterm freedom from rupture, limb occlusion, type I or III endoleak, and re-intervention.
sections.results: Of 310 patients (mean aneurysm diameter 54.8 ± 10.0 mm), 288 (92.9%) were elective. Among these, 154 (53.5%) had a standard access and 134 (46.5%) a hostile access. The latter were more frequently women (16.4% vs. 6.0%; p = .009) and more frequently had peripheral arterial disease (31.6% vs. 16.8%; p = .006). Elective technical success was 100%, with no thirty day deaths. The thirty day MAE rate was higher with hostile access (8.2% vs. 1.3%; p = .032), mainly from access related events and blood loss > 1 000 mL (3.7% vs. 0.0%; p = .021), as was early re-intervention (3.7% vs. 0.0%; p = .021). At 3 years there were no aneurysm related deaths; freedom from limb occlusion was 97% vs. 100% (p = .025) and from type I OR III endoleak was 98% vs. 100% (p = .18) in the standard and hostile access groups, respectively.
sections.conclusion: The Minos ultralow profile endograft was safe and effective for the treatment of elective abdominal aortic aneurysms. Peri-operative morbidity was higher when the iliac-femoral access was hostile, and limb occlusion, type I - III endoleak, and re-intervention were more evident compared with standard access anatomy. An ultralow profile platform can extend endovascular repair to unfavourable access vessels without affecting midterm device performance.

items.title: Cilostazol and Risk of Major Adverse Limb and Cardiovascular Events after Revascularisation for Peripheral Artery Disease.

sections.objective: Patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) remain at high risk of major adverse limb events (MALE) and cardiovascular events (MACE) after revascularisation. Cilostazol, a phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor with antiplatelet and antiproliferative effects, reduces re-stenosis but its real world impact on clinical outcomes is uncertain. This retrospective, nationwide, propensity score matched cohort study evaluated the effectiveness and safety of cilostazol on MALE, MACE, and all cause mortality after lower limb revascularisation for PAD.
sections.methods: Using the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database, patients who underwent lower limb revascularisation for PAD from 2010 - 2023, with follow up through 2024 were identified. Patients with prior cilostazol use were excluded. 1:1 propensity score matching (n = 5 464 per group) adjusted for baseline differences. Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing risk models were used to evaluate outcomes. The comparison reflects cilostazol used with or without background antithrombotic therapy.
sections.results: Cilostazol use was associated with significantly lower risks of MALE (78.7 vs. 154.0 events/1 000 person-years; subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] 0.50; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.46 - 0.53) and MACE (97.9 vs. 117.1 events/1 000 person-years; hazard ratio [HR] 0.84; 95% CI 0.79 - 0.89). All cause mortality was also reduced (116.0 vs. 127.6 events/1 000 person-years; HR 0.91; 95% CI 0.86 - 0.96). Major bleeding did not differ significantly between groups (SHR 0.90; 95% CI 0.81 - 1.00), although the absolute rate was high in both groups (12.1% vs. 13.1%). Subgroup analysis showed greater limb benefit in patients not on other antiplatelet agents.
sections.conclusion: Cilostazol after PAD revascularisation was associated with lower risks of limb and cardiovascular events and mortality. These effects were observed without any increase in the rate of major bleeding, although this rate was high in both groups. Randomised trials focused on cardiovascular events are needed.

items.title: Differences in Clinical Presentation of Chronic Pelvic Pain Caused by Iliac Vein Obstruction Impacts Referral Pathway, Time to Diagnosis, and Post-stenting Pain Resolution.

sections.objective: Iliac venous stenting improves chronic pelvic pain (CPP) caused by iliac vein obstruction (IVO). Signs and symptoms vary, but this pain is reproducible and easily identifiable. However, patients can experience significant delays in diagnosis and treatment. This study aimed to determine associations between the referral history, clinical presentation, pain characteristics, and stenting outcomes among women with CPP due to IVO.
sections.methods: This was a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data of women who were referred to a vascular surgeon with signs and symptoms of IVO, including CPP, and who underwent iliac venous stenting. Associations between clinical presentation (signs, symptoms, pain severity), medical and referral history, and stenting outcomes were compared between three patient groups based on number of other specialist consultations prior to stenting (none, one, or at least two).
sections.results: Data were for 113 women (46.5 ± 15.7 years) who had CPP for 6.3 ± 6.6 years with initial severity of 6.7 ± 2.3 (out of 10). CPP was reproducible for all women, with exercise, standing, and intercourse being the most common triggers. More than two thirds had lower limb pain, oedema, and varicose veins. At a median of 7 years post-stenting, the latest pain score was 0.8 ± 1.6, and approximately 80% had full pain resolution. Women who had seen at least two other specialists had the worst initial pelvic pain, the most prescription pain medication, back pain, other abdominopelvic signs and symptoms, and previous interventions, and the fewest varicose veins. These women had 8.5 ± 7.9 years to diagnosis, but 99% still had significant improvement in, and 66% had full resolution of, their pelvic pain.
sections.conclusion: All patients had a reproducible pattern of venous origin pelvic pain, but those with worse CPP, more abdominopelvic symptoms, and less varicose veins had a more complex and delayed referral pathway and the lowest pain resolution.

items.title: Long Term Results of Surgical Treatment of Chronic Venous Thoracic Outlet Syndrome: A Single Centre Experience.

sections.objective: This retrospective cohort study with cross-sectional analysis aimed to evaluate the surgical and long term functional outcomes of a structured treatment algorithm for patients with chronic venous thoracic outlet syndrome (cVTOS).
sections.methods: Patients with cVTOS and treated at this tertiary centre between 2016 and 2024 were included. Treatment consisted of transaxillary thoracic outlet decompression (TOD), venolysis, and subclavian vein (SCV) recanalisation. In case of persistent venous obstruction during the primary procedure, anticipated repeat percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) was planned. Anticoagulation (rivaroxaban) was prescribed until 48 hours before surgery, resumed the day after surgery for six weeks, or until 48 hours before re-PTA. The primary endpoint included SCV patency and secondary outcomes included functional outcomes (DASH and Derkash scores).
sections.results: Seventy patients were included (mean age 35 years; 56% women). Median time to presentation was 40 (20.0 - 104.0) months after initial upper extremity deep vein thrombosis (UEDVT). Eleven patients (16%) had an operative complication (haematoma n = 6, pneumothorax n = 1, UEDVT n = 1, transient Horner syndrome n = 1, phrenic nerve injury n = 1, and SCV rupture n = 1). Median length of hospital stay was 1.0 day. Venography post-TOD/PTA showed persistent venous obstruction in 15 patients (21%) for which re-PTA was planned. Over time, 20 patients (29%) developed re-stenosis. A total of 35 (50%) re-PTAs were performed. Primary patency was 56%, primary assisted patency was 86%, and secondary patency was 93% at last follow up (12 months). Median post-operative DASH score decreased significantly (pre-op: 32.9 (15.8 - 48.3) vs. post-op 8.0 (2.3 - 27.8); p < .001) with a mean follow up of 45.7 ± 27.5 months. Zero patients reported a poor Derkash score.
sections.conclusion: Chronic VTOS can be effectively treated with good long term functional outcomes. Re-PTAs were necessary in half of the cases (anticipated). This treatment algorithm diminished the need of secondary interventions in 50% of the cases, as well as the need for long term anticoagulation usage.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of camrelizumab plus docetaxel and carboplatin as neoadjuvant therapy for stage II-III triple-negative breast cancer: the HELEN-Trio 011 randomized clinical trial.

sections.objective: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy has become the standard-of-care for stage II-III triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC); however, anthracycline-containing regimens are associated with considerable toxicity. We evaluated camrelizumab combined with an anthracycline-free docetaxel-carboplatin regimen in this setting.
sections.methods: We performed a multicenter, randomized, open-label, phase 3 trial at 14 hospitals in China between December 2022 and June 2025. Eligible patients were women aged 18-70 years with previously untreated, stage II-III TNBC. Patients were randomized 2:1 to receive 6 cycles of neoadjuvant docetaxel (75 mg/m2) plus carboplatin (area under the curve [AUC]=6) on day 1, with or without camrelizumab (200 mg intravenously on day 3). The primary endpoint was pathological complete response (pCR), defined as ypT0/Tis ypN0, evaluated in the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population (all patients who received at least one dose of study treatment).
sections.results: A total of 369 patients were enrolled, and 352 comprised the mITT population for efficacy analysis.
